articles.title: VOTE: Who has been the best WWE wrestler of the 2010s?
articles.summary: Just a handful of episodes of Raw and SmackDown remain on the WWE calendar for the 2010s as the bell rings on another decade of WWE.
articles.body:
The 1980s will be remembered for Hulkamania running wild, the 1990s saw the birth of the Attitude Era and the 2000s were all about Ruthless Aggression.

So how will the 2010s be remembered? We have picked out five key players from the past 10 years in a bid to find the best of the bunch.

Make your selection from this elite group of five competitors as we bid to crown WWE's top wrestler of the decade…

It is interesting to contemplate what WWE would look like today if CM Punk had never existed.

The 'Chicago made' superstar stands alone as the single most influential in-ring competitor of the past 10 years, a man whose differences from those around him drove the company to become expansive and inclusive in ways previously unseen.

There would be no Daniel Bryan, no Kevin Owens and maybe even no Seth Rollins if there had not been a CM Punk, a wrestler who proved main-event level stars did not need to be musclebound giants to become the most popular people in the business.

Such a strategy had been in place since the mid-1990s (for very obvious reasons) but no man since the days of Mick Foley had more success with it than Punk.

Today, he remains the last name on the list of stars to make a comeback. There is a great deal of romance when looking back at Punk's time, but if he remains retired, his story will stay perfect forever.

Daniel Bryan, widely considered to be the best wrestler on the planet today, made his WWE debut in January 2010 and his story has been threaded through the not-always-rich tapestry of sports entertainment for the entire decade.

Under his real name, Bryan Danielson was a star of the independent scene for 10 years prior to his WWE arrival, the American Dragon setting new standards in his Ring of Honor matches against Christopher Daniels, Samoa Joe, Nigel McGuinness and countless others.

In his early days he proved that 'indie darlings' could transition to the bright lights of WWE and carved a path which has since been followed by almost every member of today's roster.

Even neck surgeries and a forced retirement in February 2016 does not diminish Bryan's standing. He came back from all of that and finishes up the second as the best in the business, seamlessly transitioning from face to heel and back again.

Not many wrestlers will leave the legacy that Bryan does - and he's still going strong on a nightly basis.

For the vast majority of his career, AJ Styles was cast in the role of the 'one that got away' from WWE, enjoying a long association with TNA and following that with a spell in Japan in which some of his best work was done but during the autumn of his career.

Styles made his WWE debut at the 2016 Royal Rumble at the age of 38 and with more than 17 years of experience as an in-ring competitor under his belt.

At the time, the more critical observers in wrestling saw the move, somewhat cynically, as a final payday for a man whose best years were behind him, but Styles has proved such scepticism wrong by continuing to perform at the highest of levels.

Now aged 42, he accepts there are very few years ahead of him and this year commented he has now signed his final contract in sports entertainment.

But even today there is nobody quite like Styles, as a 'seller' of moves and as a man capable of captivating the crowd's attention either as a heel or a face.

As someone who is neither a much-loved favourite from the independent scene or a highly-skilled veteran overlooked for far too long, Roman Reigns' inclusion on this list is very eye-catching.

But you simply cannot argue with the man's record. He was part of the enormously-popular Shield faction, eliminated 12 people at the 2014 Royal Rumble and then won the event in 2015, and is a triple crown and Grand Slam champion.

Reigns has headlined WrestleMania four times - from 2015 to 2018 - and has been right at the top of the company's merchandise sellers throughout that time.

He will forever be affected by his long positioning as 'the guy' the company pushed hard to succeed, and even after recovering from leukaemia the booing for that has not entirely subsided.

In the ring, he may be the weakest worker on this list, but there's no denying Roman Reigns has been a hugely important figure in WWE in the 2010s.

AJ Lee and Paige may have stronger claims from a legacy perspective, and Ronda Rousey made an enormous splash in her 12 months in the business, but Charlotte Flair has won 10 women's titles and has been the dominant female force of the past decade.

A competitor schooled entirely in the NXT laboratory and with no independent experience whatsoever, Flair is a total product of the current WWE farm system and marries that background with the DNA of being the daughter of one of the greatest of all time.

Flair will almost certainly overtake her father's record of 16 world title, having amassed 10 in the space of four-and-a-half years.

Throw in the small matter of a history-making WrestleMania women's main event and the impact Flair cannot be understated.

Who is your selection for the WWE wrestler of the decade? Vote here...

articles.title: Geraint Thomas: Former Tour de France winner signs contract extension with INEOS Grenadiers
articles.summary: Welsh cyclist Geraint Thomas has signed a new contract which will keep him as part of the INEOS Grenadiers team for another two years; the 2018 Tour de France winner hinted at possible retirement on the conclusion of the contract, but is still ambitious to compete at the highest level
articles.body:
The 37-year-old Welsh rider finished second in this year's Giro d'Italia and won the Tour de France in 2018. He has been a consistent performer in France since his maiden victory, finishing second in the race in 2019 and third in 2022.

Thomas hinted at a potential retirement upon the conclusion of the contract too.

"Although you 'never say never', in my head this is my last contract - but I know that I still have two more big years in me - and I wouldn't have continued in a different team," Thomas, who has spent 14 years with the team, said.

"This team understands me and, importantly, knows what it takes to achieve success... We're an ambitious group and have some big goals ahead.

"I'm really looking forward to getting stuck in again and want to help the team continue to progress."

Outside of cycling's Grand Tours, Thomas' other road-racing successes includes victories at Paris-Nice, Criterium du Dauphine, Tour de Suisse, E3 Harelbeke, Volta ao Algarve em Bicicleta, Bayern-Rundfahrt and Commonwealth Games gold.

He is also a double Olympic champion on the track, having won gold medals at the Beijing and London Games.

Thomas is ambitious to remain competitive in future races but added he would also be willing to help younger talent break through.

"I want to continue to be highly competitive in anything really," Thomas said. "Maybe look at going to the Classics again or ride [for the general classification] in Grand Tours or help whoever is going to be the next guy coming through, but I just want to have a positive impact on the team.

"I'm at that stage where I'm still hungry to perform but at the same time, I am happy to help the team. I want to try and help us push forward to get back to the very top of the sport."

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan beats Barry Hawkins 6-3 at Masters snooker to secure semi-finals place
articles.summary: Seven-time Masters champion stays on course for a first title since 2017 with quarter-finals win over Barry Hawkins in scrappy but closely-fought match; O'Sullivan to meet either Jack Lisowski or Shaun Murphy in Saturday's semi-final
articles.body:
While neither player was at their best in Thursday afternoon's first quarter-final, it made for an entertaining and close match with Hawkins, the 2022 finalist, initially leading 3-2 before O'Sullivan took back control of the match to move 5-3 clear.

O'Sullivan, chasing a record-extending eighth Masters title but first since 2017, was 50-0 behind in the ninth frame as his English compatriot attempted to avoid defeat but a missed red in the right-hand middle pocket proved to be match-ending for Hawkins.

The seven-time world champion returned to the table and sealed the winning frame with an impressive break of 77, which included a sensational but expertly controlled long pot on the final red.

Missed chances proved to be Hawkins' undoing with the match having appeared to decisively turn in the seventh frame when the No 15 seed missed two pinks off the spot. O'Sullivan, despite his own missed red into the bottom right, eventually made his shots count to move 4-3 ahead, and the 48-year-old never really looked back.

O'Sullivan will now face the winner of Thursday evening's quarter-final, Jack Lisowski vs Shaun Murphy, in the semi-finals on Saturday.

"I just feel sorry for Barry," said O'Sullivan in his interview immediately after the match.

"He was playing good until he started playing me and I just dragged him down to probably the most awful standard of snooker.

"So I'm really sorry about that today but I'm just lucky to get through is all I can say."

The two quarter-finals on the other half of the draw take place on Friday.

Judd Trump, the reigning champion, is up first against Ali Carter in the afternoon session before Mark Allen, the 2018 victor, takes on three-time winner Mark Selby in the evening.

Shaun Murphy managed to keep a resurgent Jack Lisowski at bay as he beat him 6-3 in Thursday's evening session to reach the last four of the Masters for the first time since 2020.

A clearance of 133 and doubling the final black saw Murphy lead 3-1 at the interval before he produced another 123 break after the restart.

Lisowski reduced the deficit to 5-3 but ran out of position off the pink in the ninth frame while Murphy held his nerve and claimed the victory to set up an O'Sullivan showdown.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan masterclass sees him past Ding Junhui to reach World Grand Prix final
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan eases past Ding Junhui 6-1 to book World Grand Prix final spot; Masters champion and commentator Alan McManus: "I've seen it and I don't believe it. It was mind-boggling. It was one of those 'I was there' nights because frankly it cannot get any better that that"
articles.body:
Even by O'Sullivan's standards, one week after sealing a record-extending Masters title, he produced a special display at the Morningside Arena in Leicester, which included four quickfire century breaks.

When he sank the final black to set up a meeting with three-time winner Judd Trump, the match was a little over 70 minutes long.

O'Sullivan made a superb start, making two centuries in the opening three frames to lead 2-1, with his potting close to perfection

He opened with a break of 135 and, after Ding responded with a score of 85 to level it up at 1-1, O'Sullivan followed up with a 128.

He made a break of 88 in the fourth frame to open up a 3-1 lead, with all four frames before the interval taking just under 45 minutes.

Ding, who beat compatriot Zhang Anda 5-1 to book his semi-final place, was under pressure, but after being given a chance at the start of the fifth frame, he faltered when on 28.

O'Sullivan ruthlessly punished him, compiling a score of 90 to motor 4-1 ahead with an average shot time, up to the end of the fifth frame, of 14 seconds.

Ding erred on a tricky safety shot early in the sixth frame and O'Sullivan stepped in to rattle off his third century - 128 - to lead 5-1 after one hour and four minutes.

He pounced on another Ding mistake in frame seven and faultlessly cleared the table for a final break of 124.

Match commentator and former world champion Ken Doherty told ITV4 that it was the best session of snooker he had ever seen.

Doherty said: "He's such an artist, such a genius. It's artistic, poetic, it's balletic. It's like snooker from the gods without a shadow of a doubt."

Co-commentator and former Masters champion Alan McManus added: "I've seen it and I don't believe it.

"It was mind-boggling. It was actually one of those 'I was there' nights because frankly it cannot get any better that that.

"From the very start to the very end it was perfection."

articles.title: Netball Super League: England's Jess Shaw targeting NSL final after return to Loughborough Lightning for 2026 season
articles.summary: England and Loughborough Lightning's Jess Shaw has set her sights on a successful year for club and country; watch the Netball Super League live on Sky Sports this season, with Loughborough Lightning facing LexisNexis Dragons at 6pm on Saturday
articles.body:
Having left the Lightning in 2020, Shaw has had successful spells with Team Bath, Severn Stars and Birmingham Panthers but now returns to last year's Netball Super League runners-up as a far more polished player.

Ahead of her side's season-opener against LexisNexis Dragons on Saturday, live on Sky Sports , Shaw set out her goals for the year, which features the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow across July and August.

"This squad is really exciting," Shaw told Sky Sports .

"They've been in finals now for five consecutive years, so hopefully we get into that final again this year.

"With it being a Commonwealth Games year, for me, coming to Lightning is going to help me perform. I've got the team behind me and if I am performing, I'll be out on that court."

Her return got off to an encouraging start as the Lightning started the year by winning the Super Cup over the weekend.

Shaw also explained that some of the thinking behind her move to Loughborough was that she will get playing time across both the wing attack and centre positions.

She added: "Coming into a Commonwealth Games year, it's really important that I am at the top of my game and playing across both positions, so hopefully I can get that this season."

Shaw's rise to the top of the sport is made all the more remarkable by the fact she was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes as a teenager.

The 29-year-old still has to manage her health carefully but finds motivation in showing younger people with the condition that they can succeed in elite sport.

"I still find it really challenging living with Type 1 diabetes," Shaw said. "It still catches me off guard depending on different games and things.

"But over the years I have started to get a bit more to grips with what works for me on gamedays, and training around that.

"But again, some days it's just out of my control and I'm really struggling to kind of get it in that range.

"For me, it's just doing it for the ones that are younger and look up to me as a role model, to know that even living with Type 1 diabetes, it doesn't stop you and when you do get to the top it's actually a lot sweeter."

articles.title: Alicia Scholes hits back at critics after London Pulse edge LexisNexis Dragons in physical Netball Super League battle
articles.summary: 2025 champions London Pulse narrowly beat LexisNexis Dragons 51-50 in Netball Super League; Pulse wing attack Alicia Scholes faced criticism over push against Victoria Booth
articles.body:
Last season's treble winners faced last year's bottom-placed side with Pulse securing victory by a single point with a 51-50 win on Friday night.

But in what was a very physical game with 96 penalties called, Scholes felt the brunt of the criticism for a push against LexisNexis Dragons' Victoria Booth in the final quarter.

Scholes took to her Instagram to address those criticising her, responding to some tweets, and posting the infamous message of former Manchester City forward Mario Balotelli - 'Why Always Me?'

"So you can get constantly shoved for 60 minutes off the ball then one push back and that's all people want to talk about," Scholes wrote.

"Twitter please talk about how good Jacqui Newton was or something. Bored to tears of seeing my name on that app.

"To the nice people, I love you so much.

"I'll read anything and never care, but you lot have my mum crashing out.

"She's 50 guys, she doesn't need the stress and she's sensitive."

The 24-year-old expressed feeling targeted for her actions while the physicality of play from others was ignored.

Throughout the game it was evident that both sides were pushing the limits on 'non-contact' as many teams have done in recent years as the physicality of netball has grown.

Lisa Alexander, who had coached the Australian Diamonds for nine years and won two world cups, also took to X to briefly express her thoughts that the debate online had been unfairly focused on Scholes.

Another notable moment that was highlighted was when Dragons' Georgia Rowe appeared to grab Darcie Everitt's ankle after the pair clashed while contesting for the ball late on.

Prior to this weekend's games London Mavericks head coach Tamsin Greenway and former England head coach Tracey Neville discussed how the physicality of netball has developed both in the NSL and internationally on Sky Sports' Off The Court podcast .

"If you're going to make contact, make sure it's worthwhile, a really good one, just make sure it's worthwhile," Neville said.

"Players now, man up, 60 minutes, they love it. I absolutely love that challenge, that build up, that momentum.

"If you'd have seen our changing room prior to going out on an Suncorp Super Netball court, there was rugby bags in there.

"If you look at the midcourt when they're preparing now at the international level, and to be honest I didn't really hone in on other teams, but particularly us, we're grappling.

"A lot of our warmup is about grappling, ways of getting your arms out, ways of making yourself available, moving away."

articles.title: England Netball head coach: Five contenders who could lead Roses into next World Cup
articles.summary: Following Jess Thirlby's resignation and Anna Stembridge's appointment as interim head coach, the question has loomed as to who will lead the side into the world cup in 2027; take a look at five of the coaches that could take over with hopes of leading the side to another podium
articles.body:
Stembridge will lead the side into the Commonwealth Games this summer, but interviews for the permanent head coach role will promptly take place after its conclusion as the team build towards the Netball World Cup in 2027.

Thirlby had been head coach for nearly seven years, leaving a significant gap for her permanent successor who will be appointed after the Commonwealth Games with just one year to go until the Netball World Cup in Australia.

Tracey Neville had been a popular choice amongst fans after her success with England. During her tenure, the Roses won England's only Commonwealth gold but she has ruled herself out of the running .

Tamsin Greenway was another potential choice to take on the role, with a great background as a player before moving into coaching where she has coached the Scottish national team and is currently head coach for London Mavericks.

However, Greenway recently signed a long-term deal with Mavericks where she will continue to lead the NSL side.

So with just four months until the Commonwealths, where Stembridge will take charge, and then Thirlby's permanent replacement appointment, who are some of the potential choices?

Now the interim assistant coach on a secondment from her role with Loughborough Sport, Olivia Murphy is an interesting option to become head coach as she would come with a wealth of experience as a player, coach, and sport director.

Murphy is one of England Netball's most notable players with 95 international caps, she also captained the side at the 2002 and 2006 Commonwealth Games as well as the 2003 World Netball Championships.

As a coach she has been part of the Loughborough Lightning set up since its inception and served a stint as the side's head coach, seeing the team grow into the dominant force it has been in recent years.

However, despite her extensive experience within the sport - Murphy has not taken on a head coach role for quite some time, so stepping into the role with only year until the Netball World Cup could be a challenge.

Sharni Layton is England's current specialist defensive coach, a role she has held with the Roses since 2024.

A two-time Netball World Cup winner with Australia and Commonwealth Games gold medallist, Layton brings extensive international experience and crucially a unique perspective to the England set up.

Australia has always dominated world netball, with 12 Netball World Cup titles and four Commonwealth Games golds, an insight into how to tackle the Diamonds in their own backyard could be crucial.

However, while England Netball are looking for a change, bringing in a non-British coach could be beyond their aspirations for now.

Alternatively, England may look to former international Jo Harten, who is joining the coaching team as a specialist coach for the Commonwealth Games but is also based in Australia within the New South Wales Swifts' coaching team.

The former England international retired from playing last year having spent the final nine years of her career at Giants Netball, who are based in Greater Western Sydney, and served as the sides' captain for five years.

While she is only at the very beginning of her coaching journey, she is an interesting option with her wealth of experience within both the England set up and domestic leagues abroad.

In her current role with Swifts, she is coaching some of the best attackers in the world at the moment, England's Helen Housby and New Zealand's Grace Nweke.

Although appointing her as head coach of England in, what would be, just one year after retiring may be too ambitious for now.

Sonia Mkoloma is very familiar with the England set up having served at the England Netball Pathways head coach before leaving to coach Birmingham Panthers this year in the Netball Super League.

Prior to her pathways role, Mkoloma was also assistant coach to Thirlby and played a key part in England's historic silver medal at the 2023 Netball World Cup.

Last year, she led the junior roses to bronze at the Netball World Youth Cup to close out her time in the role.

She will be very familiar with many of the current and upcoming Roses due to her time within England, so could be a reliable option to lead the side with very little preparation time.

As a player she also represented England at five World Cups, taking home three bronze medals, and three Commonwealth Games and earning a total of 123 caps.

Mkoloma also spent a lot of her domestic playing career in Australia for Swifts after a short stint in New Zealand's top league, the ANZ Championship

Some may also recognise her from being a referee on Gladiators, and has spoken previously about how she would love to see netball sell out arenas just like the tv show does, so could her possible head coach appointment help build towards that?

Sara Francis-Bayman, the England international with 84 caps, is also another option for head coach post Commonwealth Games.

She is also currently based in Australia where she has taken up the role of General Manager at West Coast Fever after two years as Assistant Coach for the club and Scotland.

But she was also part of the Loughborough Lightning coaching team after retiring in 2017 for four years, including two full seasons as head coach, and led the side to their maiden NSL title.

Francis-Bayman's insight from down under within one of the Suncorp Super League's top teams last year would potentially shake up the style of netball played in the England squad to improve their chances at challenging Australia and New Zealand.

She also works with England captain, Fran Williams, and Sasha Glasgow at Fever which could aid a smooth transition if she were to take the role.

Some of Jamaica's best players have also worked with Francis-Bayman at Fever, also allowing a potential insight into how they could surprise the Sunshine Girls and disrupt their game.

Overall her combined experience as a player and coach would make her a great choice of England head coaches, but Francis-Bayman may not wish to move away from the sunny coastlines to take the role.

Particularly as her side came very close to a SSN Premiers title last year, losing to Melbourne Vixens by just one point, she may want to stay with Fever and keep developing the team there.

articles.title: Beau Greaves for the Premier League? 'There is no ceiling - she's still getting better', says Laura Turner
articles.summary: Beau Greaves continues to smash the glass ceiling after winning her first PDC ranking title on Monday; Laura Turner believes she can transition her form from the floor onto the bigger stages; you can watch Premier League Darts live on Sky Sports every Thursday
articles.body:
The 22-year-old from Doncaster won seven straight matches in Milton Keynes which included a sensational deciding-leg victory with a 142 checkout over 'Bully Boy' in the showpiece to seal a landmark victory in darts history.

The two-time Women's World Matchplay champion took down a trio of former World Champions en route to the title, including Rob Cross, Gary Anderson and Smith in her final three matches of the event.

"I was glued to it," Turner told Sky Sports . "I'm sure she does feel pressure. She's human and she implied in her interview afterwards that she doesn't get to pull those 142 finishes off under pressure, but she doesn't show it.

"We all wax lyrical about how beautiful her throw is, it's so smooth but she uses it to perfection.

"She started to have deeper and deeper runs on the ProTour and there must have been some expectations because she's picked up a record 53 Women's Series titles since the middle of 2022, which is just unbelievable, but it's now transferring it to the next big thing.

"She's won on the Challenge Tour, Development Tour, and now she's won on ProTour, so I can see it happening, but for it to happen so quickly into her first year on the ProTour, that's something really impressive."

Turner believes her victory on Monday will be a catalyst for winning more ProTour titles, despite Greaves admitting to being in complete shock.

"She's not doubting her ability because you have to put in performance after performance after performance at that level and she has maintained it," Turner said.

"Everyone is super proud of the progress she is making on the oche but she's a great person off it.

"I think there is no ceiling to what she can achieve because she's getting better and her goal now is to take what she's doing on the floor, keep maintaining that, and try and transition that onto the bigger stages."

The World Youth Championship runner-up has made a seamless adaptation to life as a PDC Tour Card Holder, and her latest breakthrough win takes her to within £4,000 of the provisional qualification spots for October's World Grand Prix - live on Sky Sports .

She has also landed a brace of nine-darters in 2026 - the most recent of those coming on the Development Tour on Friday.

"She's shown signs of being able to take her form to the next level on TV," said Turner. "I'm a big believer that when it becomes less scary she will start picking up more wins. How many deeper runs can she have? She's just won a ProTour title. The sky's the limit for her."

Webster: A huge win for Greaves - her confidence to win more will now be huge

Speaking to Sky Sports News on Tuesday, Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster said of Greaves:

"It's incredible, she's an incredible player and an incredible person and do you know what, I'm not massively surprised.

"I was expecting her to win a Pro Tour during the year, I must admit I thought maybe at the back end of the year when she's a bit more settled and players are not entering the events as much, but it was a brilliant display and that reaction told you everything.

"How much it meant to her and just the level of performance throughout the day, she ran an average throughout the day above 98 and was super consistent.

"She's picking up where she left off and it was just a brilliant display, a brilliant final as well. She'll keep going now, she's making massive strides in the sport.

"She's a likeable person, she's good to watch, I really like her action, it's so natural, and to think there were issues with her release a few years ago. She seems to have addressed it, she's won a Pro Tour now and that'll fill her with self-confidence and belief that she can go on and win more.

"She's just under £20,000 off the Match Play and that's with six months of the tour she hasn't played yet, so if she could gatecrash that, that'd be some achievement.

"But what she achieved yesterday was brilliant. The manner in which she beat Rob Cross in a quarter-final - a last leg decider and he was averaging 105 - dismantling Gary Anderson in the semi-final.

"She's a proper player and look I'm not surprised how well she's started. Maybe winning a Pro Tour this early, okay I'm a little bit surprised, but she's been brilliant for the sport the last few years and it's great to see her mixing it on the main tour.

"She's got a great mentality and obviously got belief in herself. She stood up to the oche and knew it was a big moment [a 142 checkout to win the title] and it was just perfect. Michael Smith in the background, he knew it was going and he was part of a special game and pushed Beau all the way.

"The next tick of the box is maybe try and win a European Tour - she hasn't qualified for it yet, but I'm sure she will - and then it's about if she can win a major event and you' wouldn't be surprised if she did."

Speaking on Sky Sports News , Michael Bridge said: "If she carries on doing well in these ProTour Events she could qualify for some majors but nothing can stop her. The only person is herself because she has said she prefers playing against other women.

"She's absolutely dominated the Women's Series and now that she's won this it could really push her on to win more ProTour titles.

"She's a phenomenal player and I'm really looking forward to seeing how she gets on over the ProTour for the next few years.

"We had Fallon Sherrock winning matches at Alexandra Palace while Lisa Ashton won a Tour Card, but unfortunately during COVID it all had to stop. But we'll be seeing a lot more of Beau Greaves over the next few years. She is such a special, special, talent."

An emotional Greaves said after her victory on Monday: "I never thought I'd win one of these. Never, ever.

"I'm so happy. I can't even describe the way I feel. It's unbelievable and I feel so proud of myself.

"I never thought that I'd come in here today and win this. I know I've got the ability to do so, and I know I've got the talent for it, but to play the players I'm playing... I beat Gary Anderson - I couldn't believe it!

"I don't know what's happening. I'm beating players that I've watched growing up, it's just amazing.

"Aside from winning Lakeside [three-time WDF women's world darts champion], this is my best ever achievement, and hopefully I can kick on now and do well on the television.

From beating Littler to overcoming dartitis - 'Greaves has talent to beat anyone'

Greaves has made serious waves since making her PDC women's debut in 2023 with Wayne Mardle calling her "world class" then, and Turner equally complimentary as to her sheer talent since.

"We know she's got the calibre to get past anyone," Turner said previously. "You only have to look at the Youth World Championships. She beat Luke Littler in the semi-finals 6-5. Luke Littler, the world number one!

"She had a deep run in the UK Open as well, beating ProTour players, running Luke Humphries close in a longer length format. So she has most definitely got the game.

"We saw her move into doing the Development Tour, doing the Challenger Tour, picking up titles on the floor, qualifying for the Grand Slam, absolutely obliterating most players in the Women's Series.

"She's done it incrementally since struggling with dartitis a few years back. That's a distant memory now and she's just built herself up and up. I think the way she's done it, there's a lot to be admired.

"There's a lot of players who are younger now who feel like you have to race into getting to the very top of the game because you've seen the likes of a Luke Littler do it. Beau's done it gradually and she's done it to suit her situation. And I think it's great."

Last October, at the time of Littler's defeat to Greaves, he posted on X: "I had two 10-dart legs, missed double 12 for a nine and still couldn't win. Fair play to Beau. All the best in Minehead. Some talent."

Luke Humphries said at World Grand Prix in November: "I think she's an amazing player and she deserves it.

"I predict that she'll flourish playing in it [PDC ProTour].

"She's been a really great player on the secondary tours this year. She's good on the challenge tour, good on the development tour and she'll be a real threat going forward for all the players. Not just for me but for everyone.

"I think she'll do really well. If she's relaxed and she's got no pressure on her shoulders yes, I believe she will be top 64 within the two years for sure."

articles.title: Beau Greaves: Have we seen the last of Doncaster star on the PDC Women’s Series? 'I'm focused on my Tour Card'
articles.summary: Beau Greaves opens up on playing the men and insists she must improve her stage game after winning the Women's World Matchplay in Blackpool; you can watch the BoyleSports World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports from September 28 to October 4 at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester
articles.body:
Greaves claimed her third Women's World Matchplay title in four years as she edged out Fallon Sherrock 6-5 in a thrilling final in Blackpool .

The Doncaster arrowsmith kicked off her title bid with an assured 5-1 triumph over Finnish star Kirsi Viinikainen before surviving a scare against Gemma Hayter.

Greaves set up a winner-takes-all clash with Sherrock in the final with 'The Queen of the Palace' taking back-to-back legs to level at 5-5 and force a decider.

They shared maximums but Greaves came out on top with a checkout of 56 to secure the crown.

Greaves has won a record 57 PDC Women's Series titles and discussing her future, the 22-year-old spoke about the difficulty of spinning between the men's and women's game.

"It's tough really," she said. "I think I've tried to just focus on the men's side, on my Tour Card. I think after the last Women's Series, I felt a bit deflated after it.

"I didn't really enjoy it too much. I just felt a bit like everybody wanted me to lose, so coming out of there I was like 'maybe I should just focus on playing better darts and more competitive darts and my ranking', just give me something to work towards.

"I think in the ladies game gets a bit stale for everybody because you're working towards this target and once you're there, there's nothing else to go towards.

"After the last one I was just thinking, 'I think now I'll concentrate on the Pro Tour and the Euro Tour that I've qualified for', just try and do that.

"I still love that side of the game, but now I think my main goal is the men's side and enjoy that part of it and the challenges that come with it."

Greaves' latest glory is only just the start with the World Youth finalist admitting she has got to focus on improving her stage game.

"I play darts for enjoyment but now it's my job, but I love the game. I cannot get enough of it, and to be able to support the ladies' game is a massive thing," said Greaves, who became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title with a historic 8-7 victory over Michael Smith in the Players Championship 11 final.

"I want to play even better. I win tournaments on the floor, but I think my stage game has got to improve and I know that."

Greaves' victory on the Winter Gardens stage also secured her place in the 2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts and the 2027 Paddy Power World Darts Championship, after having featured in both tournaments last year.

"Obviously winning a Pro Tour really put me in the rankings. I've done well, quarter-finals, semi-finals, but it's tough," said Greaves.

"I think I'm really enjoying the challenge just to get there, to qualify for them and yeah, it'll be an achievement for me just to play there and just to say I have done it.

"I want to win, I want to do well, I need to work harder, I want to play better. I know I've got a long way to go before I'm really, really competitive with the men.

"I know I can do it, I just have to work harder for it and just put my mind to it, just believe in myself more than anything. I think sometimes I just doubt myself too much and it gets in the way of stuff.

"I enjoy the Pro Tour, the Euro Tour coming up, I look forward to them and it's tough, but it's good."

Greaves also sent out a warning to her rivals, saying she "never surprises herself" and she can "beat anybody" on her day.

"I think with me, it's just when and where it's going to turn up and that's something that is not a very good point in my game is that I am still very inconsistent, but I can be very consistent. It's just one of those things," said Greaves, who made more history on the PDC Pro Tour after qualifying for both the Hungarian Darts Trophy and Czech Darts Open .

"I know I can do it, I think sometimes I just get very happy in my own life and sometimes I forget that I need to do better, keep winning, keep doing that to prove to get up the rankings. I get very settled and that's my problem really."

"I will definitely take the positives," insisted Sherrock, who fell short in a last-leg decider in the showpiece for the second consecutive year.

"If somebody had said to me I'd get to the final, I'd have bitten their hand off.

"Beau deserved to win. She was the better player, so full credit to her.

"Hopefully this kickstarts my season. My main aim is to get to the World Championship, so if I can regroup my game, you never know, I might go on a run again."

articles.title: Luke Littler: What does rest of 2026 look like for world No 1 as he targets the clean sweep of majors after World Matchplay triumph
articles.summary: Luke Littler is targeting a clean sweep of majors in 2026 but what exactly does he need to still win? He has already won the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League, Masters and the Matchplay in 2026
articles.body:
"The next nine days will decide if I go to the Players Championship Finals," Littler told Sky Sports on opening night.

"If I don't win this then I'm not going back to Minehead for the Players Championship Finals. If I do win this then I will have to go to some Pro Tours and try and get in there."

Littler has long talked about his hope of completing the clean sweep of majors in 2026, which hinged on a triumph in Blackpool. He completed that triumph and then some with a record-breaking 18-9 win over Gerwyn Price , setting a new record average in a final of 111.53.

He also broke his own record for the number of 180s hit across the tournament, improving his 64 in 2025 to 66 in 2026.

The victory in Blackpool saw Littler become only the fourth player in tournament history to win back-to-back titles, and the first in a decade to achieve the feat.

It was not just his performance in the final that astounded. He averaged over 109 against Niko Springer, backed that up with a 113 average plus a nine-darter against Nathan Aspinall, averaged 109 again against Josh Rock, then demolished Dirk van Duijvenbode to get into the big dance once again.

Now, he has his sights set on racking up major after major to ensure not just that he holds them all, but he holds them all in one calendar year.

In 2026, he has won the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League, Masters, and now the Matchplay.

Well, instead of a holiday to Spain, he will head off to Leicester...

What does he need to do on the Pro Tours?

As part of the clean sweep, Littler will have to defend his Players Championship Finals win in Minehead at the end of November.

However, he has not yet qualified for that tournament.

Littler currently sits £22,500 off qualification and there are 10 Players Championship events remaining in 2026.

The world No 1 has ruled out heading to Hildesheim on July 28 and 29 which means his next opportunity to try and secure qualification will come on August 25 and 26 at Players Championship 27 and 28 in Leicester.

There are then two more events in Leicester on November 4 and 5 with Littler indicating that he is likely to use these four to try and qualify.

Based on 2025, plus factoring in the increased prize money, the projected cut-off looks to be around £30,000.

At each event, there is £15,000 on offer for a title, with £10,000 for the runner up and £6,500 for a semi-final.

Taking all that into account, it looks like Littler would need to win at least one final and make another final but there is a scenario in which he may need to win a couple of these events.

Of course, what other players achieve at the remaining 10 events all will get factored in but Littler will know at least one victory and a good run is required.

The next job on the list for Littler is the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam on September 17-20.

Littler came within one victory of retaining his title after losing out to Michael van Gerwen in Amsterdam in 2025.

The previous year he won the tournament by beating Michael Smith 11-4.

Then back to Leicester... for the World Grand Prix!

The next PDC-ranked TV major is the BoyleSports World Grand Prix from September 28 - October 4 at the Mattioli Arena, Leicester, live on Sky Sports .

Littler returns as defending champion after last year's victory over Luke Humphries in the double in, double out event.

By this stage, Littler will have attended two of his Players Championship events so will know how close he is to Minehead qualification.

The one he is missing: European Championship

There is also one major alluding Littler in his collection at the moment, the European Championship, which takes place on October 22-25 in Dortmund.

Gian van Veen stunned Humphries in a dramatic 11-10 victory to claim the first major trophy of his career in 2025.

Littler, meanwhile, bowed out at the last-16 stage in a 10-7 win over James Wade.

By the time Littler heads to Wolverhampton for the Grand Slam of Darts on November 14-22, live on Sky Sports , he will have had all his opportunities to qualify for the Players Championship Finals.

Littler went back-to-back at the Grand Slam with an imperious 16-11 win over Humphries.

Making it three in a row is the next requirement to continue his target.

If Littler has done what he needs to on the Pro Tour, then a trip to Minehead on November 27-29 is the penultimate piece of the puzzle.

Littler secured a win in 2025 with an 11-8 victory over Nathan Aspinall in the final.

If 'The Nuke' backs up at Minehead, after completing the ridiculous list above, then there is just one more task.

How Littler would love to make it three in a row on darts' biggest stage in order to complete the season haul and run into 2027 with back-to-back clean sweeps in his sights.

In 2025, he beat Van Gerwen. In 2026, he beat Van Veen.

If he were to cap off a spectacular year in the most spectacular of fashions, he would become the first person since Phil Taylor in 2006 to win the title three times on the spin.

"I have always said, I have got to win 16 Matchplays, 16 worlds, and then have a look at whatever else Phil Taylor did win," Littler said.

An unprecedented trophy haul would be a good start.

articles.title: Beau Greaves first woman to win match on PDC European Tour, plays Luke Humphries next at Czech Darts Open
articles.summary: Beau Greaves rallies from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in first round of Czech Darts Open as she gets revenge from first-round defeat to 'Superchin' in 2026 World Championship; European Tour win another first for Greaves this year; Niko Springer to face Luke Littler in Prague
articles.body:
The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday afternoon.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.

She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest despite averaging 104 but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after pinning double one to defeat Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Championship.

Greaves 'loving the experience', will 'be ready' for Humphries

Greaves said after a contest in which she won three straight legs in 14, 13 and 11 darts: "It feels amazing. It's just so nice to win a game, I was so nervous at the start, I don't know why. It took me so long to get settled.

"It means loads to me, the crowd's fantastic. It's such a tight stage and you feel so much from the crowd. I'm really enjoying it and loving the experience."

The Yorkshirewoman showed tremendous fight to respond from an early two-leg deficit once Gurney produced a 144 checkout - the same finish which had helped him see off Greaves at Alexandra Palace late last year.

On facing Humphries next, a player she met at the 2025 UK Open, Greaves added: "I've played Luke on the big stage before so I know what to expect, he's world class so I'm going to have to play a lot better than I did tonight.

"What more do you want than on a Euro Tour to play one of the best players in the world? I'll look forward to it and I'll be ready."

Elsewhere on Friday, Niko Springer averaged 102 while routing Martin Homola 6-0 to book a second-round meeting with world No 1 Luke Littler.

Springer said of his showdown with Littler: "I have nothing to lose to be honest. I'm feeling very confident. Of course it will be hard, but it's best of 11, so let's go, I'm ready."

Joe Cullen, Dirk van Duijvenbode and Cross were big-name casualties, dumped out by Stephen Burton, Mario Vandenbogaerde and Keane Barry respectively.

Humphries, who, like Littler, received a bye to round two as one of the 16 seeded players, has won the last two Czech Darts Open titles, thrashing Kim Huybrechets 8-1 in the 2024 final and then seeing off Josh Rock 8-5 last year.

'Cool Hand' is targeting a fourth victory in five years at this event having overcome Cross 8-5 in the 2022 final.

articles.title: Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur blasts 'erratic, poor' performance as side fall to defeat ahead of play-offs
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos lost the last two rounds of the regular season ahead of the Super League play-offs; They await to find out their semi-final opponents; The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
In what was effectively the battle for the League Leaders' Shield, Wigan Warriors wiped the floor with Leeds in a 40-8 drubbing.

Wigan then completed the formality and wrapped up the domestic double with a 50-12 win over Catalans, keeping a treble firmly in their sights.

Meanwhile, Leeds finished with an 18-12 loss to Hull FC who will finish the season in 11th. It is not the time to run out of steam - Leeds now have a week's rest to figure out how to reset, recharge, and head into the semi-finals reinvigorated.

They will know who they face once Wakefield Trinity play Leigh Leopards on Friday September 18 and Warrington Wolves face Hull KR on Saturday September 19 in the Eliminators, live on Sky Sports .

They need to welcome their semi-final opponent to Headingley and make them feel like they are entering a fortress.

Leeds head coach Brad Arthur admitted that very element was missing in Round 27 and said it was simply "not good enough".

"We were a bit erratic at times. Some of our skill with the ball was very poor," Arthur said.

"We created more than enough opportunities. More than enough field position. Our forwards did more than enough on our edges and we were poor on our edges without execution."

It is clear that Arthur knows what the issues are but is there an easy fix?

He believes that will be down to individuals stepping things up and making sure, for one final time in 2026, that Headingley is too tough for whoever has to visit to ensure Leeds make it to Old Trafford for the first time since 2022.

"It's an individual thing. Our skill was poor. We created enough chances and had enough field position," he added.

"We have two weeks, new competition. But we're not happy with our performances at home. Not good enough. This place needs to be a tough place to come and play."

Wilkin: Leeds were shown their vulnerabilities and have not recovered

One thing that is key in sport is confidence. Leeds have had that in abundance until they have not.

It is a frailty laid bare by meeting a team who have been there, done that, and got the t-shirt in Wigan.

Leeds have not walked the walk in a very long time, their last Grand Final win coming back in 2017, and it is now "concerning" that they have not bounced back and that their coach believes it is a "skill and execution" issue.

"Leeds have strutted through the season with the confidence of looking like champions and feeling like champions," said Sky Sports Rugby League's Jon Wilkin.

"Last week I saw vulnerability and a weakness exposed by Wigan, who went straight over the top of them and said: 'You might well believe you're the business, but you're not'.

"It's just not happened for them. It's concerning.

"Wigan have got a deep confidence and history of being near the top. I don't think Leeds have got that yet. A champion team would react to such a humbling defeat to Wigan. Not only that, but I just don't think you get beaten so comprehensively."

"What will be a worry is Brad Arthur has highlighted skill and execution, saying that's the problem," added Sam Tomkins.

"That's the reason why they've been top for so long, they were good at the start, but they've not had it in the last month.

"If their execution is off and their skill and edge is off, that's what they hang their hat on. I think It's a worry. It's not an easy fix and there will be questions asked and it will be a tough couple of weeks."

The 43-year-old, who last tasted continental glory at the European Darts Matchplay in Hamburg in 2016, produced a 95.50 average and five 180s in the final in Antwerp on Sunday evening.

Earlier in the day he'd beaten Damon Heta 7-4 in the semi-final, having whitewashed Danny Noppert 6-0 in the quarter-finals and edging Rob Cross 6-5 in the last 16.

"Some weeks it's good, sometimes it's bad. That's how it is for me," he said after claiming the £35,000 prize money.

"If it was good all the time, I'd smash them all to bits. We can't always select how we feel."

Wade played in the first European Tour final in Austria in 2012 and this win means he was victorious in the 150th event.

Smith, who won the Hungarian Darts Trophy two weeks ago, beat Gian van Veen, Ryan Joyce and Gerwyn Price in last-leg deciders earlier on Sunday.

"I rode my luck today and the players have let me off, but Wadey, doesn't let you off ever," Smith said.

"I admire him. I watch his game and I can only admire the guy.

"James thoroughly deserved the win today. He's just-he's absolutely class, isn't he?"

articles.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield set for special Super League Grand Final duty: Bringing it back to 'where it started' for Rob Burrow
articles.summary: Kevin Sinfield to present match ball at the Grand Final at the conclusion of his latest, and final, running challenge to raise money for the MND community; watch the play-offs all the way through to the conclusion at the Grand Final on October 3 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The former Leeds Rhinos and England captain is preparing to embark on his latest gruelling running endeavour, raising further awareness and funds to support the MND community across the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.

Sinfield, who has helped raise more than £11m for the MND community with his team since his first annual challenge in 2020, will complete an ultra-marathon every day for seven days.

Starting at the home of world club champions Hull KR on Sunday September 27 and visiting each of the home grounds of the 12 English Super League clubs, he will finish at Old Trafford ahead of the Grand Final on Saturday October 3.

And now Sinfield, who led Leeds to seven Grand Final glories at the Theatre of Dreams, will present the match ball in readiness for the current-day gladiators to do battle.

For Sinfield, this final running challenge is a special opportunity to bring it all "back home" to the rugby league community and visit some venues at which Burrow thrived.

Not only that, Old Trafford is where Burrow scored arguably the best Grand Final try in 2011 against St Helens, and for Sinfield that makes the Theatre of Dreams a particularly fitting end.

"I think it's nice to bring it back home to the rugby league community. This is where it all started for Rob," Sinfield told Sky Sports .

"To visit some venues where he terrorised opponents is particularly special and to finish at Old Trafford is great.

"Rob scored, in my opinion, the greatest Super League try, greatest Grand Final try ever. He won eight Grand Finals.

"To get a chance to visit some places that I know very well, where the support has been awesome over the last six years, I am looking forward to it.

"We were here (Old Trafford) for the Rugby League World Cup final in 2022 and the support we got that night was immense considering England weren't in the final.

"We were all hoping and expecting, so it doesn't matter which teams are in the final.

"I think the love for Rob, the support, the love for the MND community will shine through and I am incredibly proud of the way rugby league has come together again and continues to do, to look after it's own, and it will be a really special night."

RL commercial managing director and interim RFL chief executive Rhodri Jones added: "Sir Kevin is one of the most iconic names in Super League history.

"He is synonymous with Grand Final night and his remarkable endeavours, all those epic running challenges we have seen over the years in support of his great friend Rob Burrow and the MND community, remain an inspiration to us all.

"As a competition, we are delighted he's now bringing the ball to the centre stage at Old Trafford ready for the biggest 80 minutes of the season when everything is on the line and the latest Betfred Super League champions are crowned.

"The whole sport of rugby league wishes Sir Kevin and all his team the very best on what promises to be yet another arduous and challenging seven days."

Six charities are set to benefit from this year's fundraising. The work of the MND Association , Leeds Hospitals Charity , My Name5 Doddie Foundation , Darby Rimmer Foundation , MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association will once again be supported by the challenge.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Ross Smith thrashes Gerwyn Price in final after Luke Littler's dream of clean sweep ends
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price "does not care" if he never wins another major as he prepares to head to Tenerife following "absolute rubbish" defeat to Ross Smith in World Series of Darts Finals; Luke Littler knocked out in last eight as hopes of clean sweep of titles dashed
articles.body:
Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.

Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4 , the Welshman, who only struck five 180s, said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family and I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

"I was absolute rubbish in that final but don't take anything away from Ross. He was brilliant and took his opportunities."

Smith stars in Amsterdam as Littler crashes out

While Smith celebrates his fifth trophy of the season - this triumph in the Netherlands follows the Hungarian Darts Open and International Darts Open on the European Tour and a couple of Players Championship events - Littler is processing a shock defeat.

Having won the first six majors of the year - including the World Cup of Darts for England alongside compatriot Luke Humphries - Littler was hoping to claim all 11, only to be trounced 10-4 by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

Smith overcame Josh Rock 10-7 in the semi-finals before dumping out remaining home hope Gian van Veen 11-8 in the last four, while Price surged towards the end of matches to eliminate James Wade and Clayton 10-7 and 11-7 respectively before being floored by Smith.

Smith said: "It feels a bit mad, to be fair! I am absolutely made up with the win. I am so happy. [Price] is one of the best in the world, so to beat him you have to up your game.

"I always say in my interviews that I take each game as it comes. I play one game at a time. They are all finals and I give it my all. That is working for me at the moment."

Smith followed a 123 finish in the 11th leg with a 127 in the 12th as he stormed to victory from 5-5.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 2 Booms and Busts: Bears offense does a complete (and ugly) 180
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski highlights the winners and examines the losers of Week 2's Sunday action.
articles.body:
Just a week ago, it looked like the Chicago offense was headed to the moon. It turns out the moon is a harder commute than we realized.

Variance and weather can be major headaches in the fantasy football space, but injuries are without question the ultimate killjoy. The Minnesota at Chicago game was a cocktail of all three annoyances, a 9-3 win for the Vikings and a nightmare for fantasy managers.

The Caleb Williams injury was the unquestionable Sunday headliner in Week 2. Williams suffered a non-contact right-leg injury in the fourth quarter and immediately we braced for the worst. The team eventually announced that Williams had a hamstring injury, and there were reports of Williams walking under his own power — albeit with a limp — after the game.

Williams isn't out of the woods yet, but at least we can exhale. Nobody can adequately play doctor watching from a television, but it sure looked like Williams was dealing with a long-term injury — perhaps a season-ending injury — when the fateful play occurred. We'll see what we learn when Williams goes through a battery of tests. Hopefully he can still play for a chunk of the 2026 season.

Even if Williams has to miss time, it's possible that head coach Ben Johnson could cook up something interesting with backup Tyson Bagent . It's also fairly likely that Bagent will be needed to make some starts, beginning with Week 3 against Philadelphia .

No matter who the quarterback is, Johnson needs to get his passing game cooking. It was easy to write off last week's curious production split (the signature pass catchers did almost nothing) as a fluke. But now Luther Burden III (3-32-0 Sunday), Rome Odunze (3-43-0) and Colston Loveland (1-3-0) are sitting on two straight washout games.

Of course, the other teams get paid, too, and Brian Flores runs a potent, blitz-happy defense with Minnesota. And three hours of wind and rain put a damper on both teams. But this is not the Chicago offense we dreamt about all summer. Loveland was drafted to be a slam-dunk weekly starter, and Burden and Odunze were seen as ascending talents with high ceilings. And for the second straight week, the Big 3 was outproduced by unheralded receiver Kalif Raymond (5-40-0).

Minnesota's offense was stuck in the mud Sunday, too. The wind blows funny for everybody. Aaron Jones Sr. made 103 yards on 23 carries, handed the backfield to himself, and Justin Jefferson cobbled together a 3-55-0 line on six targets. It's still possible this offense can be functional with Carson Wentz , but a bad-weather day in Chicago doesn't offer a definitive conclusion.

The upcoming schedule looks friendly enough. Minnesota takes on Tampa Bay, Miami and New Orleans the next three weeks.

Carolina home to the surprise fantasy carnival of 2026

How do we cleanse our fantasy palate? A trip to Carolina should turn the trick. The Panthers rolled over the moribund Falcons, a 34-3 laugher that was never competitive.

Could it be a breakout year for Bryce Young ? He's feasted on perfect matchups, but they don't hand out 287 passing yards and three touchdowns at the airport. Young wasn't intercepted and only took two sacks.

He's got plenty of help downfield. Tetairoa McMillan (5-101-0, 10 targets) is a legitimate alpha and Jalen Coker (8-66-0, nine targets) an ascending secondary receiver. Darren Waller (3-33-2) popped in the red zone. Young also threw a touchdown to Chuba Hubbard , who did his normal thing — 64 somewhat boring yards, one score and a double-digit fantasy day.

Carolina should find running room in Week 3 at Cleveland , and the leaky Lions defense visits in Week 4. Sounds good to me.

The Atlanta defense is a gigantic concern, of course. Michael Penix Jr. has never been a decent pro, but he'll be needed as the eventual savior. Cooper Rush (32.6 rating, two picks) and Jack Strand (35.1 rating, one pick) were both awful Sunday.

Somehow Bijan Robinson was able to grind out 81 total yards, and Drake London 's 4-51-0 line isn't that bad given the circumstances. But this is a team with look-out-below potential. Kyle Pitts Sr. logged a 1-15-0 day on three targets. We'll have a close look at the mess over the next three weeks, as the lovely schedule makers have Atlanta playing consecutive games in prime time. Green Bay (Thursday), New Orleans (Monday) and Baltimore (Sunday), come on down.

New Orleans is going to be a fun team this year. Last week's overtime loss at Detroit stuffed the box score, and the passing game traveled to Baltimore, scoring an upset. Tyler Shough had 252 passing yards and two total touchdowns, and he kept the downfield concentration to three main targets ( Chris Olave , Juwan Johnson , Devaughn Vele ). I'd start any of these guys against anyone.

The one buzzkill in New Orleans through two weeks is Travis Etienne Jr. , who's run nowhere and been forced to share (last week with Kendre Miller , this week with Alvin Kamara ). Normally following the money will lead you to good fantasy decisions, but the big Etienne contract has not lead to the meaty role that many envisioned.

The Patriots didn't break records in a 20-3 win over Pittsburgh , but it was a nice bounce-back for several key players. Romeo Doubs got loose for 3-96-0 on four targets, Drake Maye averaged 9.5 YPA (though he had one bad pick), and TreVeyon Henderson (16-76-1) hit the ground running in his first 2026 action. Henderson's role might have expanded after Rhamondre Stevenson (46 total yards) lost an early fumble. Challenging games at Jacksonville and Buffalo come next.

We spend almost a week trying to find a breakout receiver in Houston , someone who could ascend in Nico Collins ' absence. Turns out it was TE Dalton Schultz who fit the assignment. Schultz went bonkers (12-140-0, 14 targets) in the loss to Cincinnati , while no one else in the offense topped 37 receiving yards. Xavier Hutchinson at least was liberally targeted, drawing nine looks for the day (a 3-37-0) return. The slumping Texans head to Indianapolis next.

The Eagles had to be more aggressive after an early-game Saquon Barkley injury, and ultimately Jalen Hurts and friends did enough to hold off Tennessee . DeVonta Smith had the type of target-hog game we've been hoping for (10-117-1) and Dontayvion Wicks (5-74-0) was active for a second straight week. Hurts only ran for 16 yards on five attempts, but 264 passing yards and two scores validated the game. The Eagles should score liberally against Chicago next week.

Nobody stood out in the Green Bay backfield, but it's interesting to note that MarShawn Lloyd barely saw the field after a second-half fumble. At least Lloyd already had a touchdown catch in the bank, saving his day. Kaleb Johnson (8-32-0) had the best foot of the three Green Bay runners, and it was frustrating to see the passing game struggle against an unheralded Jets defense. Christian Watson only returned 4-41-1 on an 11-target game, but the touchdown saves the day. Tucker Kraft (2-15-0, three targets) isn't up to speed yet, and Jayden Reed was carted off with an early-game neck injury.

I don't want to pile on Tony Pollard , because I think he's still a decent back. But game script ruined his Week 1 story, and on Sunday he was held without a touchdown while Cam Ward stole a couple of short-yardage scores. Pollard ultimately ran 14 times for 64 yards, and had a short reception. Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton combined for 11 carries in support, so this backfield might be more crowded than we anticipated a few weeks back.

articles.title: "As a kid growing up in Northern Ireland, I dreamed of winning all four majors": How Rory McIlroy went from a young boy with a golf dream to a $350 million superstar at the top of his sport
articles.summary: International Sports News: Rory McIlroy’s rise from a young golfer in Holywood, Northern Ireland, to one of the richest names in the sport is tied closely to a dream he had as a.
articles.body: Rory McIlroy’s rise from a young golfer in Holywood, Northern Ireland, to one of the richest names in the sport is tied closely to a dream he had as a child. Today, Celebrity Net Worth estimates McIlroy’s fortune at $350 million, built through prize money, endorsements and other earnings. The figure tells only part of the story. His parents worked multiple jobs to help fund his golf development, giving him opportunities that eventually turned an early talent into a global career. Now, with six major championships and 30 PGA Tour wins, McIlroy has reached a level few could have imagined when he first picked up a club.How did Rory McIlroy build his $350 million net worth?Rory McIlroy’s financial rise began long before the huge sponsorship contracts arrived. Celebrity Net Worth says his family was not particularly wealthy, but his parents found ways to pay for the training and travel needed to support his ambitions. His father, Gerry, also played an important role in developing Rory’s game. By age seven, McIlroy had become the youngest member of his local golf club.That early investment eventually produced major results. McIlroy turned professional in 2007 and won his first PGA Tour title at the 2010 Quail Hollow Championship before turning 21. A year later, he won the U.S. Open. The PGA Championship followed in 2012, then the Open Championship and another PGA Championship in 2014.The money grew with the success. Celebrity Net Worth estimates McIlroy has earned more than $115 million in PGA Tour prize money, more than €50 million on the European Tour and millions more through FedEx Cup bonuses. The PGA Tour currently lists his official career earnings at $119,555,515.Endorsements have been an even bigger part of the financial picture. McIlroy has had major partnerships with Nike, TaylorMade, Omega and other global brands. Celebrity Net Worth estimates he has earned $40 million to $50 million annually from endorsements in recent years. The site also reports that he is vesting into roughly $50 million in PGA Tour Enterprises equity.What did Rory McIlroy mean when he talked about his childhood dream?The emotional weight behind McIlroy’s fortune became clearer when he reflected on the four majors after completing the career Grand Slam. He wrote on social media:“As a kid growing up in Northern Ireland, I dreamed of winning all four majors. Being able to bring these trophies home was truly surreal.”That dream is no longer just a childhood memory. McIlroy won the Masters in 2025 to complete the career Grand Slam, becoming the sixth male golfer to win all four majors. He then won the Masters again in 2026. The PGA Tour now credits him with six major championships and 30 PGA Tour victories.There is a striking gap between the young boy whose parents worked extra jobs to support his golf and the businessman-athlete whose fortune is now estimated at $350 million. articles.title: Dacia Sandero Hybrid 155: una apuesta por el sentido común
articles.standfirst: El Dacia Sandero pone en escena su versión híbrida, un motor imprescindible para un modelo de éxito. Un nuevo argumento para seguir siendo líder del mercado
articles.summary: El Dacia Sandero pone en escena su versión híbrida, un motor imprescindible para un modelo de éxito. Un nuevo argumento para seguir siendo líder del mercado.
articles.body: Es el coche más vendido en España, con diferencia. Se agarró con fuerza al mercado en 2007 con un precio súper competitivo y un concepto que parecía hecho a medida de una de las crisis más importantes de las últimas décadas. En ese contexto Dacia ofrecía una solución de movilidad, austera, sencilla y sin lujos, pero muy asequible. Muchos vieron en el Sandero una salida al problema de movilidad en muchas economías familiares que se encontraban muy deterioradas. Fue un salvavidas para muchos y se quedó como una opción para los que quieren ser más prácticos. Si el Dacia Sandero era en sus inicios un coche que podía ser algo primitivo, las diferentes evoluciones lo han puesto al día. Es cierto que también ha subido algo su precio, pero sigue siendo una opción para los que buscan una solución práctica. Ahora es un producto mucho más actual en diseño, tecnología y confort. Esta fórmula está visto que funciona porque no ha dejado de encabezar las listas de ventas llegando a vender 400.000 unidades hasta hoy. Ahora se incorpora por primera vez la mecánica hybrid 155 que se pondrá a la venta el último trimestre del año. Esta motorización permite al vehículo arrancar en modo eléctrico y reducir de forma importante el consumo en ciudad ya que es capaz de circular durante un 80% del tiempo en cero emisiones. El sistema híbrido combina un motor 1.8 litros de gasolina y dos motores eléctricos que logran alcanzar una potencia de 155 CV. De esta forma se consiguen unos consumos de 4,2 litros /100 km. y unas emisiones 96 g/km. de CO2 (4,4 litros/100 km. en el Stepway). Este propulsor se combina con una caja de cambios automática multimodo que resulta muy eficaz. El motor desarrollado por el centro de I+D+I de Horse Powertrain en Valladolid es una gran opción para aquellos que no quieren el paso al eléctrico puro ya que se trata de un motor con un funcionamiento muy suave y eficiente que resulta perfecto para un uso diario en entornos urbanos (que es donde consigue muy bajos registros de consumo) por un precio muy asequible (19.890 como precio de acceso). Dacia acierta con esta nueva propuesta que ya se echaba de menos en su gama. Puede que sea la alternativa más interesante en un mercado muy dividido por las diferentes opciones energéticas que se presentan. La etiqueta ECO, un comportamiento eficiente y un precio muy competitivo completan una oferta que parecen renovar una fórmula que ya ha sido ya todo un éxito. Al mismo tiempo que llega la nueva motorización al Dacia Sandero, Duster y Bigster también estrenan un nuevo sistema Tribid 150 4x4. Este motor, también desarrollado en Valladolid, es realmente novedoso al combinar tres fuentes de energía: electricidad, gasolina y GLP. Se asocia con una transmisión que funciona en 4x2 y 4x4 desarrolla 150 CV de potencia y logra una autonomía, según el fabricante, que alcanza los 1.500 km en el Duster, gracias a dos depósitos de gasolina y GLP de 50 litros cada uno. Esta es una tecnología no se había conocido hasta el momento en ningún otro motor y supone una aportación relevante al mercado. En combinación con la caja automática de doble embrague de seis velocidades resulta una alternativa segura, económica y eficaz. La utilización del GLP reduce el coste por kilómetro en combustible en un 30% respecto a la versión anterior. El motor Tribid 150 pone al Duster y el Bigster en unos registros de consumo realmente competitivos. En cuanto a los precios, el Duster arranca en los 27.790 euros y el Bigster en 30.890 euros. Estas novedades tienen más relevancia de lo que parece en un principio ya que atacan directamente lo que supone el corazón del mercado. Este tipo de motores son ahora una de las opciones más seguras en el contexto energético en el que nos movemos ya que son ahorradores, con buen rendimiento y con algunas ventajas con su etiqueta ECO por sus bajas emisiones. De hecho es posible que se convierta en la opción más interesante de los que se deciden por la marca rumana.

articles.title: Granit Xhaka breaks silence after fake Covid vaccine certificate claims spark Swiss investigation and potential 5 years of jail time
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka has issued a public apology after admitting he obtained a Covid-19 vaccination certificate despite not receiving the v.
articles.body: Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka has issued a public apology after admitting he obtained a Covid-19 vaccination certificate despite not receiving the vaccine. The Switzerland international is now under investigation by the Lucerne public prosecutor’s office over the matter.Xhaka, 33, has also withdrawn from Switzerland’s upcoming Nations League fixtures. Swiss authorities are investigating whether the certificate involved forgery or falsification of documents. The offences can carry a maximum prison sentence of five years under Swiss law, although reports suggest a custodial sentence is considered highly unlikely in Xhaka’s case.Granit Xhaka admits mistake and agrees to cooperate with authoritiesGranit Xhaka was playing for Arsenal when the incident allegedly took place in 2022. He has now accepted responsibility for his actions and said he will cooperate fully with the investigation.The Sunderland midfielder released a statement on Monday after reports about the case emerged.“In recent days, a lot has been reported about an issue from my past. I would like to address it personally. At the time, in connection with the Covid-19 vaccination, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns. I had deep distrust of the vaccine and was affected by fear and uncertainty”, he wrote.“In this emotionally charged situation, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of having my unanswered questions clarified through the proper channels. Today, I clearly see that this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry. I take responsibility for the decision, will face the process of clarifying the facts, and will cooperate fully with the relevant authorities”, he added.According to Swiss authorities, the investigation is being handled by the Prosecutor’s Office of the Canton of Lucerne. Authorities are examining whether Xhaka was involved in behaviour linked to a possible false notarisation or falsification of documents.The authorities also stressed that Xhaka is presumed innocent while the investigation remains ongoing.The Switzerland captain is expected to appear before the public prosecutor’s office next month.The Swiss FA has also confirmed that Xhaka will not take part in the upcoming international camp. The decision was reached jointly after discussions between the player and federation officials.Peter Knäbel, president of the Swiss FA, said Xhaka informed the federation about the situation and wanted to take responsibility.“Granit Xhaka informed us about the situation last night and told us that he will address it publicly and take responsibility,” he said.“We welcome Granit taking this step and facing the consequences. At the same time, we jointly concluded that it is in the team’s best interest to complete this training camp without him. Our priority now is to calm the situation and focus entirely on the team and the upcoming challenges in the UEFA Nations League. After the conclusion of this international match window, we will reassess the situation together with Granit and discuss the next steps”, he added.Xhaka will therefore miss Switzerland’s upcoming fixtures involving North Macedonia, Scotland and Slovenia.The midfielder joined Sunderland in 2025 after leaving Bayer Leverkusen.
