articles.title: What happened when Arber Xhekaj watched Florian Xhekaj fight during the Montreal Canadiens NHL preseason
articles.summary: NHL News: The Montreal Canadiens began their NHL preseason with two split-squad games against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday, Sept. 19. Arber Xhekaj skated.
articles.body: The Montreal Canadiens began their NHL preseason with two split-squad games against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday, Sept. 19. Arber Xhekaj skated with the Montreal group at Bell Centre, while Florian Xhekaj joined the Canadiens squad in Toronto.The brothers were at the heart of one of the night's more strange moments. Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Marshall Rifai fought Florian at Scotiabank Arena while Arber was serving a two-minute roughing penalty in Montreal.Arber Xhekaj watches Florian Xhekaj fight during NHL preseasonArber Xhekaj saw his brother Florian Xhekaj’s fight from the Montreal Canadiens bench after a staff member showed him the footage on a phone during a stoppage in play. Sportsnet cameras caught Arber leaning over to watch action from the other preseason game.The two Montreal Canadiens groups were in different cities playing at the same time, so Arber couldn’t watch Florian’s fight live from the ice. In between whistles, a staff member pulled out a phone and showed Arber the footage.He watched the fight immediately, and I was fired up seeing it, Arber said after Montreal’s 4-3 overtime win. He also texted Florian afterwards.What happened between Florian Xhekaj and Marshall Rifai?Florian Xhekaj was in the fight with Marshall Rifai, as Montreal takes down the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-1 in Toronto. Younger Xhekaj also recorded an assist, adding another notable contribution during an important preseason opportunity.Florian is battling for a regular NHL roster spot after spending the majority of last season with the Laval Rocket. He played in five NHL games last season, but his physical game has still been a big part of his game.Montreal won a pair of split-squad games against Toronto, taking a 4-3 overtime victory at Bell Center and a 4-1 decision at Scotiabank Arena. Montreal’s Cole Caufield scored in overtime, and Phillip Danault scored twice in Toronto.The results also provided Montreal with a handful of preseason storylines outside of the Xhekaj brothers, including good showings from other players competing for roster spots. But the rare moment of viewing the penalty box gave Arber and Florian one of the more memorable NHL moments of the night.Arber Xhekaj found himself in an unlikely spot for an NHL preseason moment: the penalty box for the Montreal Canadiens as he watched his younger brother, Florian Xhekaj, fight. Arber was in Bell Center, Florian in Toronto, as the split-squad teams from Montreal met the Toronto Maple Leafs in different cities.During a stoppage, Arber watched video of Florian fighting Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Marshall Rifai on a member of the staff’s phone. Florian also had an assist in Montreal's 4-1 victory in Toronto, while Arber's team won 4-3 in overtime. articles.title: Ranking Every NHL Team's Home Jersey for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: With a new NHL season on the horizon and preseason games already underway, it's high time we got down to serious business when it comes to fashion. Jersey fashion, that is.
articles.body:
With a new NHL season on the horizon and preseason games already underway, it's high time we got down to serious business when it comes to fashion. Jersey fashion, that is.

While all teams are adding Hometown Remix jerseys and others are adding various alternates and throwbacks to be unveiled at later dates, the home jerseys, by all accounts, remain unchanged, so we can judge them anew. While some opinions change with time, others are hard to budge, apart from how we feel about things in the moment.

Whether your team has a classic look or something more modern, we do our part to be tough, but fair in judgment of them but with 32 teams to sort through, it's work we take a lot of pride in, just like you all take pride in telling us how wrong we are when you don't like our rankings. So please, feel free to share those thoughts with us!

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

When Reebok's EDGE style was unleashed upon fans back in 2007 or so, it brought some of the poorest-looking jerseys in NHL history. Although the Capitals showed off a great new script-based logo, the style of those jerseys was just far too busy, and they've never changed them since, despite how much we beg them to do just that.

One day, we'll get our wish, at least that's our hope.

It's not that we're big-time haters of the Panthers jerseys; it's just that what makes them unique compared to virtually every other team are things we have yet to really warm up to for 10 years now, since they changed to this style at the start of the 2016-2017 season.

The colors and striping are good; the logo is solid enough, but the patches and numbers on the shoulders say "football" more than they do "hockey." Here's to hoping their "Hometown Remix" sweaters bring the heat the way their sky-blue Reverse Retros did in 2022-2023.

We're not sinking the Predators in our rankings because of their glorious golden-yellow color or their extremely awesome Nashville logo on the front. We love both of those immensely. What's got us putting them here this year is how relatively plain the whole of the look is now.

The guitar strings on the numbers are good, and the nods to Music City like that are great, but the whole of the jersey is so simplified it kind of mutes it. "If it's too loud, you're too old," works in music and in hockey jerseys.

There's a lot to love about what's available to the Blue Jackets in terms of designs, and for as bold and brash as they were when they arrived in the NHL, they've done a lot to bring it back to earth with their home and road sets.

Although they're called the Blue Jackets, their home jerseys could use a little less blue and a little more red-and-white striping to liven them up. Maybe it could use a little more cannon, via a shoulder patch or by owning how very Ohio they are, the way they did with their Stadium Series jerseys a couple of years ago. We love you, Columbus, but you're frustrating us.

As we've shown in years past with our rankings, winning a Stanley Cup doesn't help give you a boost in jersey rankings, and the Carolina Hurricanes aren't getting much of a reprieve this year.

We know the 'Canes are in an awkward position with a primary logo that can be difficult to design around and secondary logos that make for great iconography (the storm flags on a hockey stick; Stormy the mascot in a hat and sweater out of the 1950s), but their black home sweaters with the storm flags is about as good as they've got and it's still not enough to give them a lift in the rankings. It's grown on us a little, but when we think of the Hurricanes, we're thinking of them in bright red more than black, and even winning the Cup again can't fix that.

The Lightning are a team capable of doing so much more with their jerseys, and they've done so with their alternates in recent years, but their home set, despite how clean and simple it is, is almost too plain.

We like the Lightning logo just fine, but the design of the jersey itself has borne such a resemblance to the rival Toronto Maple Leafs since they began wearing it in 2011-2012 that it's still mentally difficult to separate the comparison.

Sure, the Lightning have been far more successful with the look and have the Stanley Cups to show for it, but it doesn't make the observation any different. At least the shoulder logos give it a slightly different look and feel.

It may upset some fans to see the Kraken's superb jerseys so early in our rankings, but despite the cool colors and logos, it's a jersey that gets punished because they have a far superior alternate.

The navy-blue home sweater with the seafoam green and light blue stripes, along with that little touch of salmon red, makes us think of the ocean, and the Kraken logo is genuinely very good. The anchor shoulder logo with the outline of the Space Needle is wonderful as well. But this jersey, compared to their black alternate jersey with the green outline and menacing sleeve stripes, is just so much better.

We're not asking for that to become their primary home jersey, but we wouldn't mind hearing that it would be seen more often either.

Ottawa throwing their look back to the franchise's beginnings in the 1990s was so overdue and so necessary to get everyone back on board with them. Their black home sweaters are exact copies of what they wore from 1993 to 1995, and it's a great look.

Throwbacks can sometimes get heat for trying too hard to embrace what once was, but those Senators teams from those years weren't great, and the current team, despite recent drama, is good, and now they look good, too.

It's impressive how success can sometimes change an opinion. In the Wild's case, seeing them win more often in their regular home jerseys can help make it look better.

The dark green jersey with cream and red stripes and the Wild logo crest is genuinely good. It hammers home the fact that the team is centered on nature and the wilderness, and the look is wholly their own. Their gorgeous Minnesota North Stars-colored alternates that everyone clamors for are great on their own (and a bit better than their home jerseys), but the Wild having a very solid home jersey in their own colors is a good thing.

What we love about the Ducks' home jerseys is that their full embrace of the original Mighty Ducks logo is back, making them feel real again. We also love that they're fully ensconced in orange, and for a bold-color jersey in the NHL, that's how it should be.

Anaheim's home uniforms get routinely killed for going so hard on orange, from the helmets to the sweaters to the pants and socks, and yeah, that's definitely a lot of orange. Throw some black pants on that set and you might be really cooking there. But the jersey? That's superb even if the number and letter coloring feels off.

The Stars have had fantastic jerseys since rebranding their look in 2013, and it's such a strong style that they don't need to change it at all. Their "victory green" home jerseys with the logo on the front are superb and all you can ask for from a jersey.

If there's a modern template teams follow for designing a jersey, the Stars followed it to the letter. That's not a bad thing by any means, but after unveiling their modernized 1999 throwback alternate jerseys last season, we know there's more they can do to make things look good on the ice, apart from winning a lot of games.

We haven't held back our enjoyment of the Golden Knights embracing what it means to be a team based in Las Vegas and going full, sparkly gold with their home jerseys. After all, if you're going to be in Vegas, be all about it and they are and that's good.

Now, do we have nitpicks about how the jersey itself is styled? Sure, but they're really minor and were more of an issue when their home jersey was pewter gray and black instead of gold. We love that Vegas tries to do things differently, and a sparkling gold jersey on the Strip is exactly what we want to see.

The Avalanche are in that funny spot where their current sweaters are good, but they're not as good as what they once had.

Colorado did their part to make their jerseys look close to what they had when the franchise moved to Denver in 1995, but those originals were so good right out of the gates that they set a high bar to surpass.

Their current jerseys lean more toward lighter blue and gray to go with the burgundy body. The Avalanche logo stands out proudly, but the different-style sleeves make it unique and not at all a throwback design. It works fine, and it's definitely better than anything from the Reebok era, but it's hard to let go of those old memories of what they had before.

When it comes to our rankings, we're rather unabashed enjoyers of Original Six sweaters. They're classic, they're simple, they're virtually unchanged throughout history, and, as teams are finding out these days, what once was a great look remains one today.

So how do the Maple Leafs end up here in our rankings? It's not because we don't like their blue home sweaters. We love them and how they're iconic. We love the logo, we love blue and white, and we love simplicity. But it's so simple all the same, and they've tinkered with their look enough over time that they've been able to do more interesting things with it, even in smaller ways.

We're eager to see what they do for their centennial to celebrate it, and if their center ice design is a tip-off, we're all about it.

Detroit's home jersey is one of the most iconic in the NHL, and it's been imitated and copied at many levels of hockey. When you've got a logo like the Red Wings' winged wheel, it's really hard to mess that up. Even with all the off-ice drama surrounding the team, it can't take away from how great they look on the ice.

We could note how the jersey has been virtually unchanged since 1937, when they made the numbers totally white on the red sweater, but isn't it incredible that a change like that happened 90 years ago? You don't mess with perfection, although a perfect jersey doesn't always grant you a top-five spot these days.

Throughout the Canucks history, they've had a lot of changes to their jerseys, but their current style with the orca crashing through ice in the shape of the letter "C" with the original stick-in-rink logo on the shoulders is so clean it makes us wish the team wasn't in such a bad way.

Say what you will about the Canucks logo, but it's been their primary for nearly 30 years now (1997) and that's longer than any other logo they've had before it. The blue, green, and white color scheme is great, and the striping is clean. If you can't be good on the ice, you better look good, and the Canucks certainly do.

We'll confess to being somewhat of haters in the past when it came to the Jets' home jerseys, but time has a way of softening opinions and helping us learn to love things, and that's just where we're at.

Winnipeg's home sweater is great. The navy blue, sky blue, and white colors are great, and the sleeve striping is uniquely good. The Jets logo is a nod to both the Canadian Air Force and their ownership (True North), but it looks great. Even the shoulder logos are solid enough, and the fonts for the names and numbers are great.

Sure, it would've been simple enough to use former Jets logos and run with it to make a zillion dollars but doing that for the alternate sweaters was the right move to incorporate that and have their own identity.

When the Kings went full-on retro rebrand last season, it was really hard to argue with their use of the 1990s silver-and-black style and logo as the template. It was such an iconic look during the heyday of Wayne Gretzky in Los Angeles, establishing the Kings as one of the premier franchises in the NHL, and bringing it back full-time made sense, especially given how the team went back to black, silver, and white as their colors in 2011.

Even though the logo is just a tad different from the 90s logo, the idea is the same, and the style of the jersey is just about spot-on for what they had back in the day. It's an iconic look for L.A., one that everyone there and across pop culture can easily identify with, and that goes a long way. Even though the silver has a bit more sparkle than it used to, that's not a bad thing, given they're in Hollywood and all.

If you're not down with the Devils logo, we want to know if you're feeling OK, because that alone is worth it, no matter what style of jersey they want to put it on. Instead, the Devils have largely stuck with a redesign from 1992, when they went from green, red, and white to black, red, and white, and have left it alone for good reason.

The Devils being red and black is fitting, and while the only real changes they've made to their jerseys have been to the striping around the waist (2017 eliminated a white stripe), the appearance is essentially the same, and it's great. If you're going to be the Devils, you better look the part, and they have for decades.

Even though the Islanders will have a new alternate jersey this season, they're leaving the home and road jerseys alone, and thank goodness for that because they're perfect.

The Islanders' blue home sweater is as good and easy to look at as any sweater can be. The orange and white stripes on the sleeves and waist hearken back to their history of winning the Stanley Cup in the 80s and their successes in more recent years as well.

The Isles' iconic logo always needed to shine, and bringing back this classic style was the best way to make it shine. Call it basic if you want to, but you'll have to hear it from angry Long Islanders eager to see the glory days return.

After a full season to soak in the Mammoth's new home jerseys, it's become clear they made some great decisions in putting them together. The new logo stands out proudly on the front, and the team's color scheme since moving to Salt Lake City has been so good for hockey.

The striping on the sleeves and the Utah logos on the shoulders complement the whole look and make it really easy on the eyes. It can be hard for a new team to hammer out a look with such ease, but the Mammoth have done that, and now they've got a playoff team to watch roar around the ice in them, too.

There's an argument to be made that no jersey since the 70s has been so imprinted on the minds of sports fans as the Philadelphia Flyers' orange, black, and white sweaters. When the team went back to the burnt orange color from the 80s last season, and with Rick Tocchet at the helm, everything felt a bit more at home.

Although the new Flyers jerseys are still a throwback to the old days, old being new again works out great when it comes to Philly and hockey. The Flyers logo is among the best and most recognizable in sports and if we're going to see Philly in the playoffs, seeing them looking like this is just how we want it to be: Iconic.

Everyone knows who the Rangers are based on the color of their jersey, and when you've got that kind of recognition, you're doing things right.

The "Blueshirts" home blue sweaters with the white and red stripes are such a clean and hockey-specific look that it's impossible not to appreciate (fans in New Jersey, Philadelphia, and on Long Island excepted). The horizontal spelling of "Rangers" in the red-and-white drop-shadow text, to match the similar number-and-name-style lettering, is gorgeous.

It's hard for Original Six teams to go wrong, and the Rangers haven't gone wrong with this look since 1947. Don't mess with greatness, even if it isn't producing Stanley Cups with regularity.

Although the Sharks didn't throw it all the way back to their 90s jerseys with their rebrand in 2022, they did it in a way that made it modern and just as incredible to look at, and their home teal sweaters are spectacular.

The Sharks logo is among the best in the NHL, and a modernized version of the shark chomping down on a hockey stick is great. Bringing back the shark fin shoulder logos was a brilliant move, and simplifying the color palette by sticking to teal, black, and white (excluding gray) somehow makes it look a little cleaner and even a bit more ominous. Now that they've got Macklin Celebrini to put fear into the rest of the league, the sound of the "Jaws" theme at games ought to be a lot scarier for opponents.

Few jerseys can be truly iconic in a sport and throughout pop culture, but Chicago's home red sweaters accomplish that. Whether it's on the ice with Connor Bedard and Patrick Kane or off it in Wayne's World or National Lampoon's films, it's there, screaming hockey history at you.

A design from a much older time, it's almost certainly past its prime; that said, you'll be hard-pressed to find a jersey more associated with hockey than this one.

When the Bruins tweaked the design of their home and road sweaters last season and decided to make it look as close to their 1980s jerseys as possible, they hit it out of the park.

The Bruins' spoked-B logo is another of the many iconic logos in sports, and giving it the simple, powerful style it had during the 80s and early 90s provided the proper palette for it. A black jersey with gold and white stripes as well as the throwback Bruins logo on the shoulder, it's a real beauty and evokes all the memories of the team's past.

St. Louis' throwback blue jersey teased us when they wore it at the 2017 Winter Classic, showing how great their sweaters looked in the 60s and 70s. When they held onto that jersey as an alternate the following year, we were happy to see it stick around longer. But when they made it their full-time home jersey and, last season, the inspiration to change their road jerseys as well, we were absolutely ecstatic.

The lighter shade of blue as the base for the home jersey is gorgeous, and the way it makes the gold and white stripes on the sleeves and waist look is making us wonder why they didn't make this change ages ago, as they sorted through various designs since the Reebok Edge days. It's another case of a throwback done right and one where bringing it back was 100 percent the right call.

Speaking of throwbacks brought back for a good reason, the Penguins' black and gold jerseys from the 1980s and 90s were always among the best-looking jerseys of all time, and seeing the sweaters that Mario Lemieux and Jaromír Jágr made into a championship look in the 90s, done so again by Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin now, was just too good.

The skating penguin logo is one of the best in hockey history, and the City of Pittsburgh colors of black and yellow, paired with it, make it a "bled into the fabric of the people" kind of thing. That these jerseys were brought back in 2014 and became the team's full-time look a couple of years later made all the sense in the world.

For a time, coincidentally, during a large part of a 15-year playoff drought, the Sabres' jerseys were a bit lost in the desert. They messed around with other logos, brought back the original one but altered the colors, and generally tried to reinvent the wheel. But when the Sabres brought back royal blue and gold as their colors and returned to a jersey design closer to the original style, things changed.

The Sabres' blue home jersey, with the logo on the front and gold and white stripes, is as clean as any in the league. And while other teams may have the same colors, the Sabres' look is hyper-specific to them, and any time they match up against another team with a great look, it's bound to be one of the most pleasing games to watch.

For so long, the Oilers had some of the best and most iconic home and road jerseys in the league. Sure, they had Wayne Gretzky and Mark Messier to thank for that, winning Stanley Cups and making Edmonton the city of champions in the 80s, but their blue jersey with the orange and white shoulder yoke and sleeve stripes was synonymous with hockey greatness.

Then, for years after that, the Oilers messed around with the look and colors, trying hard to make something new for their spectacular logo. None of it compared to the original, however, and eventually those glorious 80s sweaters found their way back for Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl to shine once again. Every game these jerseys appear in makes them look better.

The foundation that Flames jerseys had established for them in Atlanta in the 70s carried over when they went to Calgary in 1980, and even though they experimented with other styles for a while in the 90s and 2000s, returning to the original style made the Flames whole again.

Their red home sweaters with the yellow and white stripes, along with the iconic flaming "C" logo, are as close to a perfect look as you'll get in sports. With a name like the Flames, you have to think of fire when you look at them, and these jerseys more than do that. It's an intimidating look when they're playing well, and even when they're not, they just look incredible, period.

How good are the Montréal Canadiens red sweaters? They've been essentially unchanged since 1925, and only when the NHL mandated names on the back of jerseys in the 70s did they change substantially. From the iconic logo to the colors to the stripes, this look is hockey.

Franchises across sports hope to have something that is so defiantly their own, like the Habs' red sweater. Yankees' pinstripes, the Dallas Cowboys' white uniforms, and the Boston Celtics' green uniforms are as close to the Canadiens as it gets, but the Canadiens' jersey defines the game itself. They're forever the No. 1 when it comes to style, and everyone else in the NHL is fighting for second place.

articles.title: Who is Yu Zidi, China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation?
articles.summary: The teen phenomenon won her second gold medal in the 200m medley in 2:06.10 to set a new Games and Asian record.
articles.body:
China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi has smashed her second Asian Games record in as many days, with her time of 2:06.10 in the women’s 200m individual medley doubling as a new Asian record.

The teen prodigy made waves last year when, aged 12, she became the youngest-ever medallist at the World Swimming Championships.

Tuesday’s win and record saw Zidi cement her status as one of swimming’s greatest teenagers and a dominant force at the ongoing Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan.

So who is Yu Zidi, and what else can we expect from her? Al Jazeera Sport explains.

The swimming sensation was born in Baoding, China, on October 16, 2012. She was noticed by a swimming coach as a six-year-old when her father took her to a water park to cool off in the summer.

How has Zidi performed at the Asian Games?

Zidi has reclaimed her Asian record in the 200m individual medley (IM) from defending champion and compatriot Yu Yiting, who clocked 2:06.82 in June and finished second on Tuesday with 2:07.99, while Japan’s Narita Mio finished third in 2:10.40.

The 13-year-old now holds the Asian Games record, the Asian record, and the second-fastest 200m medley of all time – just 0.40 seconds off the 2:05.70 world record set by Canadian Summer McIntosh, another former teen phenomenon in the sport who Zidi considers her idol.

Zidi’s gold in the 200m IM adds to her 200m Butterfly win a day earlier, where her 2:05.08 smashed the Games record of 2:05.57 set by compatriot Yufei Zhang at the Hangzhou 2023 Asian Games.

Zhang, a multiple-time Olympic, World and Asian Games champion, was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) at Hangzhou 2023 alongside compatriot Qin Haiyan for her record six gold medals. She picked up her first gold at Aichi-Nagoya in the women’s 4x100m Freestyle relay when China stormed to victory in 3:33.10.

“Very excited, very happy. It’s an achievement that shows the hard work of our team,” said Zidi. “I’m happier with the second gold medal than the first.”

She added about 21-year-old teammate Yiting: “She’s a strong opponent who motivates me to improve and work harder.”

Despite winning gold on her Asian debut, Zidi said her 200m freestyle performance “was only so-so”, adding hopes to go faster in the future.

“My technique is still slightly lacking. I need to lower my head earlier, reach further forward and improve the movement of my legs. Those are all areas that I need to work on.”

Will Zidi win more medals at the Asian Games?

Most likely, yes. Zidi can add a third individual gold on Wednesday in the 400m IM.

The teenager, however, is not listed in China’s roster for the women’s 4x200m Freestyle relay scheduled for Thursday.

Zidi became swimming’s newest prodigy when she won bronze as a 12-year-old as part of China’s 4x200m freestyle relay team at the 2025 World Swimming Championships in Singapore in August.

She followed up her laurels at the Chinese National Swimming Championships later in the year with two golds, one silver, and an Asian record in the 200m IM.

Although World Aquatics requires swimmers to be at least 14 years of age, Zidi was allowed to participate after meeting the association’s “A” standard times that she clocked at the Chinese National Swimming Championships in May last year.

What have other swimming greats said about her?

Siobhan Haughey, Hong Kong’s first Olympic medallist in swimming, said Zidi’s dominance in a wider trend in the sport.

“I think the general consensus is we have more and more great young swimmers swimming well,” said Haughey, now a relative veteran at 28.

“When Summer first started, she was also very young and swimming fast, so I think that’s kind of the trend these days.

“Hopefully, swimming well that young, you can also translate to as you get older and well into your 20s and beyond, so it’s exciting for the swimming world,” she added.

Haughey said the evidence suggests that Yu is “definitely capable of going to the LA Olympics”.

“I think she’s doing well under pressure at big meets,” she said. “I think if she wants to do it, she definitely can.”

articles.title: Egypt’s Amina Orfi becomes youngest women’s squash world number one at 19
articles.summary: Orfi, the reigning senior and junior world champion, topped the rankings with victory at the Qatar Classic last week.
articles.body:
Amina Orfi has become the youngest women’s world number one in squash after a thrilling victory in the Qatar Classic last week saw her clinch the crown and top the rankings.

At 19 years and two months old, the Egyptian eclipsed the previous record set by New Zealand’s Susan Devoy, who was 20 years and two months old in 1984.

Orfi dethroned compatriot Hania El Hammamy from world number one when she defeated the 26-year-old 3-2 in the Qatar Classic final (7-11, 11-7, 11-8, 7-11, 12-10). The victory earned Orfi her first Platinum title, third major victory and 15th win of her career.

“Sweat, tears, heartbreaks, and tons of sacrifices all for this moment,” she wrote in an Instagram post on Monday, when the official Professional Squash Association (PSA) rankings update weekly.

Orfi’s historic milestone is the latest of her outstanding year. In May, she became the youngest world champion at 18 years and 10 months when she beat then world number two Nour El-Sherbini in a thrilling five-game final at the World Championships in Egypt.

The win made her the first player to hold both the world junior and senior PSA championship titles at the same time. The PSA is the global governing body for men’s and women’s professional squash circuits.

“It feels amazing,” Orfi said after her victory in Doha on Friday.

“To become world champion and become world number one in the same year is a dream that I’ve had since I was very young and I really want to enjoy it.

“I want to just stay at this level now and keep trying to improve every day. I want to stay on top now that I’m the world number one, and I want to win a lot more titles too,” said Orfi, who has been in the world’s top three since last October.

articles.title: Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup: England name 10-player squad
articles.summary: Rob Hawkins is among five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup winners who will attempt to help England defend the trophy in Australia this autumn.
articles.body:
Rob Hawkins is among five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup winners who will attempt to help England defend the trophy in Australia this autumn.

Hawkins, Wheelchair Super League's top try-scorer this season with 70, scored four tries as Halifax Panthers completed a domestic treble by beating Leeds Rhinos to win Sunday's Grand Final.

He is joined in England's 10-player final World Cup squad by club-mates Jack Brown - who scored six tries in that final - and Finlay O'Neill.

Both Hawkins and Brown were part of the England squad who defeated France dramatically at Manchester Central in November 2022 to win the World Cup.

So too was Lewis King, who will captain England down under, plus King's London Roosters club-mate Joe Coyd and Leeds Rhinos' Nathan Collins.

Collins will be joined in the England squad by Leeds team-mate Tristan Norfolk, Roosters' Mason Billington and the Sheffield Eagles pair of Luis Domingos and Chris Haynes.

England face Wales on Friday, 30 October (04:30 GMT) in their opening match at the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup - which will be staged alongside the men's and women's tournaments.

They then face the USA on Tuesday, 3 November (07:30 GMT) and Ireland on Friday, 6 November (06:00 GMT), aiming to secure a spot in the following Tuesday's semi-finals.

The wheelchair tournament will be staged at the Wollongong Entertainment Centre, with the final on Friday, 13 November (08:30 GMT).

England head coach Tom Coyd - who led the side to their World Cup success in Manchester four years ago - said: "Every player understands what it means to wear the England shirt and the responsibility that comes with it.

"Yesterday's brilliant Wheelchair Super League Grand Final was a testament to the special community that we are privileged to represent on the world stage."

England's wheelchair squad will fly out to Australia on 22 October.

England squad: Mason Billington (London Roosters), Jack Brown (Halifax Panthers), Nathan Collins (Leeds Rhinos), Joe Coyd (London Roosters), Luis Domingos (Sheffield Eagles), Rob Hawkins (Halifax Panthers), Chris Haynes (Sheffield Eagles), Lewis King (London Roosters), Tristan Norfolk (Leeds Rhinos), Finlay O'Neill (Halifax Panthers).

articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups, Week 3: Jonah Coleman, Tank Bigsby among top targets to add
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his fantasy football waiver wire column for Week 3.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

If you've been reading this column, you're going to recognize a lot of the names featured this week. Young was my top QB add heading into Week 2, after an outstanding fantasy performance in the opener and he followed it up with another three-touchdown effort on Sunday.

The 25-year-old former first overall pick is the second-highest scoring fantasy quarterback through two games, behind only Josh Allen, with only Monday Night Football left to be played.

Jalen Coker has formed a strong receiver tandem with Tetairoa McMillan and Darren Waller is emerging as a dangerous red-zone weapon for the Panthers. The veteran tight end scored two touchdowns against the Falcons and had another called back on a penalty in Week 1.

There's no reason to think this party will stop anytime soon, with the Browns and Lions next up on the schedule for Carolina. Consider Young a borderline low-end QB1 for those matchups.

Kyler Murray is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

Encouraging people to draft Coleman in the late rounds was my mission throughout the summer and I reserved room to write about him in each of the first two waiver wire columns this season.

Stashing Coleman was speculative, since he was technically the Broncos' No. 3 back behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. However, given Dobbins' injury history (missed time in all six of his NFL campaigns) it seemed almost inevitable that a path would be cleared at some point this season. The coaching staff and beat writers also strongly suggested that Coleman was the direct Dobbins' replacement, not Harvey.

Even with all that in mind, I certainly didn't expect to see Coleman's opportunity arrive in Week 2. With Harvey sidelined due to a hamstring injury, the rookie had a chance to see the field more on Sunday. Then, Dobbins suffered a hamstring injury of his own, which paved the way for Coleman to help lead the Broncos to victory with 58 scrimmage yards and a score on 13 touches.

While we wait for updates on both injury statuses, this is your last chance to pick up Coleman … and you're going to have to spend a significant amount of your budget to do it. Don't worry, he'll be worth it. Dobbins hasn't looked particularly good this season prior to getting hurt and Sean Payton raved about Coleman throughout the preseason. He might just take this job and not give it back, with Harvey eventually returning to his pass-catcher-plus role, when healthy.

Bigsby has been one of the better one-injury away backups to have on your bench, but that became even more important on Sunday when Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger and missed a large portion of the game. Bigsby took advantage, posting 38 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Titans.

Though Barkley is headed for an early-week MRI, the initial reports seem optimistic that this won't be a serious issue.

Regardless, Bigsby needs to be rostered. If Barkley were to miss a game, Bigsby would step in as the Eagles' lead back and a potential fantasy RB2, with Will Shipley operating as a pass-catching option.

Wilson is also seeing value inflated due to a starter getting banged up. Rookie Jadarian Price is dealing with a shoulder injury that caused him to miss time in the late stages of Sunday's game.

Just like Barkley, Price is going to get evaluated over the next couple days, but the early reports suggest this isn't anything major.

With Price missing time, Wilson leapfrogged George Holani and took over as the early-down back for the Seahawks. The result was a solid 92 yards on 21 carries.

If Price is unable to suit up for Week 3, Wilson would be a borderline low-end RB2 for fantasy in a matchup where Seattle is 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Keep in mind, Zach Charbonnet is expected to return in October, so the runway is short for Wilson.

Kaelon Black is 56% rostered but would be the No. 4 RB add behind Coleman, Bigsby and Wilson, if available.

Tyler Allegeier is 51% rostered but would be the No. 5 RB add behind Coleman, Bigsby, Wilson and Black, if available.

Zach Charbonnet is 51% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

The more things change, the more they look the same — and the top of the receiver section is identical to last week.

Perhaps it was concerns about the Browns' quarterback situation that kept managers from being more aggressive in adding Boston, but all the signs were there.

The second-rounder led Browns wideouts in snaps by a wide margin in Week 1, running a route on 97% of their dropbacks. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a 46-yard touchdown in his debut.

In Week 2, he picked up where he left off with a 94% route share and an even bigger stat line of 5-95-1 on seven targets.

As I said last week, we have a long way to go before having faith in a Deshaun Watson-led passing game, but fantasy managers need to pay attention to what Boston is doing. He's an absolute must-add and a potential fantasy WR3/flex with upside moving forward.

I'm hesitant to invest in a big Tucker game because we've seen this before with the speedy wideout. During his career, Tucker has popped up for a sizable stat line once or twice per season, before falling back to earth in the rest of his games.

Keep that in mind if you're planning to chase Tucker's five-catch, 119-yard, one-touchdown result from Week 2.

With Brock Bowers likely to return next week, Tucker's volume will be even more sporadic. He still has value as a splash-week WR4/flex option, just don't let your expectations run wild thinking this will be a weekly occurrence.

Bateman filled the void left by the absences of Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist), putting up seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown versus the Saints.

Much like Tucker, I don't expect this to become the new norm for Bateman, but we might see another strong fantasy start out of him in Week 3 if Flowers remains on the sidelines.

With the Ravens traveling to Brazil to take on the Cowboys and concerns about the quality of the field already making headlines, Baltimore would be foolish to risk re-injury to their star wideout. If Flowers sits, Bateman will be a WR3/flex option with a much higher ceiling for one more week.

Devaughn Vele is 51% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Boston, if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 53% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Gadsden starting the season buried on the depth chart behind David Njoku and Charlie Kolar was a strange development after the flashes we witnessed from him as a rookie.

However, the fantasy landscape is always evolving and Gadsden is on the verge of getting another significant opportunity after Njoku (knee) was carted off and Kolar (forearm) was seen in a sling.

Meanwhile, Gadsden found the end zone versus the Raiders, which brought back memories of his breakout month in 2025, when he posted 7-68-0, 7-164-1, 5-77-1, and 5-68-0 from Week 6 to Week 9.

While I doubt he reaches that level of production, Gadsden is back in the conversation as a TE2 streamer with TE1 upside in a Chargers offense that could use a spark.

Dalton Schultz is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add, if available.

Hunter Henry is 56% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Schultz, if available.

Favorable upcoming schedules: Chiefs (34% rostered), Bills (14% rostered), Saints (1% rostered)

Here are some players you can consider cutting from your roster to free up room on your bench for this week's top waiver wire adds.

Quarterbacks: Baker Mayfield, Malik Willis

Running Backs: Rico Dowdle, Kenny Gainwell, Chris Rodriguez Jr.

Wide Receivers: Marvin Harrison Jr., Courtland Sutton, Jayden Reed

Tight Ends: Brenton Strange, Michael Mayer

Mayfield was unable to top 13 points in either of the first two games against the Bengals and Browns. Now, he'll have to take on Brian Flores' Vikings defense. Better days will come eventually, but he's just a bye-week replacement QB2.

The idea that Gainwell would be a weekly flex option, while also offering one-injury away upside has not materialized. He's managed just 33 scrimmage yards on 11 touches through the first two games. If he's still on your roster, it's just as a stash in case Bucky Irving gets hurt at some point.

Rodriguez is a limited player with no role in the passing game. Similar to Gainwell, he has just 36 yards on 12 carries. Even if Bhayshul Tuten were sidelined, Rodriguez would max out as a TD-or-bust RB3 for fantasy.

It's not happening for Harrison in Arizona. After hauling in just one catch for 33 yards on three targets in the opener, he failed to record a reception in Week 2 with only one pass thrown in his direction. The only chance for fantasy redemption might be in a fresh start with a new organization.

articles.title: El ex árbitro del que se acordó Ortiz Arias antes del derbi: "No tuvo su mejor tarde"
articles.standfirst: García Aranda habló con Vicente Ortega en 'El programa de Ortega' de RadioMARCA
articles.summary: García Aranda habló con Vicente Ortega en 'El programa de Ortega' de RadioMARCA
articles.body: José María García Aranda, ex árbitro internacional y ex director de arbitraje de la FIFA, analizó con Vicente Ortega en 'El programa de Ortega' de Radio MARCA la actuación de Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias en el derbi madrileño. El colegiado reconoció que el árbitro "no estuvo afortunado" y que "no tuvo su mejor tarde", aunque quiso separar sus errores de su procedencia. "Esto no va a impedir que en el futuro se pueda seguir produciendo, porque en realidad no es una cuestión de dónde es el árbitro", explicó. Sobre las dos acciones más controvertidas, García Aranda admitió que "esas jugadas podrían haber sido tarjetas rojas perfectísimamente" y apuntó también al videoarbitraje: "La mayor parte coincide en que efectivamente el error no se corrigió como se debió corregir". García Aranda también respondió a las palabras de José Mourinho sobre Ortiz Arias y reclamó respeto hacia los colegiados. "Cada uno tiene derecho a la crítica, pero primero hay que hacerla con respeto, hay que hacerla desde primero una autocrítica", señaló. El ex árbitro recordó que "es muy fácil descargar en el árbitro la responsabilidad total y absoluta de una derrota" y defendió que un técnico también debe analizar sus propios errores. "No es el único culpable, ni muchísimo menos, de que un equipo pierda", añadió antes de subrayar la responsabilidad de los entrenadores como referentes: "El respeto debe primar, independientemente de que la crítica es perfectamente asumible por todo el mundo". Por último, García Aranda fue preguntado por el caso Negreira y por la huella que continúa dejando sobre el arbitraje español. "Yo creo que a lo mejor es que siempre hay intereses en que no se acabe ese tema", afirmó. A su juicio, el asunto "ha perjudicado muchísimo, muchísimo, muchísimo al arbitraje" y "le ha hecho mucho daño". El que fuera responsable arbitral de la FIFA insistió en que el objetivo debe ser mirar hacia delante y reforzar la independencia de los colegiados: "Lo que hay que buscar es progreso en el rendimiento de los árbitros". Y dejó una reflexión contundente sobre la prolongación del debate: "Hay cuestiones que es que ya huelen un poco".

articles.title: 'We are extremely angry': Israel chess chief blasts FIDE for not honouring 'commitments' after Chess Olympiad forfeits | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: Israel Chess Federation chief Zvika Barkai has accused FIDE of failing to honour a prior agreement over scheduling arrangements for Yom Kip.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Israel Chess Federation chief Zvika Barkai has accused FIDE of failing to honour a prior agreement over scheduling arrangements for Yom Kippur, after both Israel’s men’s and women’s teams forfeited their Round 6 matches at the ongoing 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand on Monday. The forfeits followed a scheduling dispute over the observance of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.The trouble began over the weekend. Israel had requested an early start to their games so they could be completed before Yom Kippur began. The Singapore men's team and the Colombia women's team, their opponents in Round 5, agreed to the adjustment, and the games went ahead on Sunday as scheduled.Monday told a very different story. For Round 6, falling on Yom Kippur itself, Israel submitted a formal request to FIDE, the sport's world governing body, asking either for their games to start after 7:30pm local time or to be moved entirely to Tuesday, the tournament's designated rest day.The Netherlands and Bulgaria refuseThis time, their opponents, the Netherlands in the Open section and Bulgaria in the Women's section, declined.With no agreement reached, both the Israeli men's and women's teams failed to show up for their scheduled games, and the Netherlands and Bulgaria were awarded full points via forfeit. Footage from the venue showed the Dutch team arriving to find no opponent waiting for them.FIDE clarified that Israel had requested schedule adjustments for both rounds because of Yom Kippur. For Round 5, it sought earlier games, while for Round 6, it requested a 7:30pm or later start or a move to September 22, the rest day. FIDE said it contacted both opponents, but neither agreed, noting they were entitled to decline.Israel Chess Federation reacts to the issueThat last line, that the Netherlands and Bulgaria were within their rights to say no, is precisely where the Israeli Chess Federation's objection begins.In an exclusive interaction with TimesofIndia.com, Zvika Barkai, president and chairman of the Israel Chess Federation, said the entire situation should never have reached this point in the first place."About six months ago, when we saw that the scheduling of the Olympiad would fall on Yom Kippur, we approached FIDE and asked them to change the date or provide us with a special arrangement," Barkai said. "It was agreed in writing that Israel's games on Monday, the eve of Yom Kippur, would be brought forward and finish before the holiday began, and that today's games, on Yom Kippur, would start two hours later, after the end of the holiday."According to Barkai, the failure was not one of goodwill on FIDE's part, but of process. "We are extremely angry that FIDE did not honour the commitments it made," he said. "Instead of putting this arrangement into the competition regulations — they were afraid of negative reactions, especially during the FIDE elections — they planned to speak with the teams that would be drawn against us. In practice, they did almost nothing, and we are extremely angry with them about this issue!!"Barkai drew a sharp contrast between how Sunday and Monday's opponents responded. Of Singapore and Colombia, who agreed to the Round 5 adjustment, he was effusive."Yesterday, fortunately, the Singaporean and Colombian teams showed sporting spirit and agreed to bring the games forward. We are very grateful to them and will also know how to reciprocate their sporting gesture," he added."Today, the Dutch team, against the men's team, and the Bulgarian team, against the women's team, behaved in an unsporting manner and strongly opposed postponing the games by an hour or by a day," he further remarked. "FIDE did not enforce what had been agreed with us in advance and caused us significant harm."Barkai's frustration extended beyond the missed games themselves to how the results will now be recorded."FIDE did nothing to minimize the damage it caused," he continued. "They could at least have tried to prevent the match from being recorded as a 4–0, which will hurt us significantly in the rankings going forward. After the Olympiad, we will consider our next steps."The forfeits, recorded as clean 4-0 defeats in both sections, carry real weight in the Olympiad's standings compared to a rescheduled result that could have been contested normally.Speaking further, Barkai laid out the federation's position at length. "We understand the difficulty of allowing us special arrangements because of the restrictions associated with Yom Kippur. We hold up the sporting conduct of the Singaporean and Colombian teams as an exemplary model, and we are very disappointed by the response of the Dutch and Bulgarian federations. The truth is that those we expected to show consideration did not disappoint us," he remarked."We didn't expect too much from the Dutch, and accordingly, we were not disappointed. And finally, once again: the relationship between the Israeli Chess Federation and FIDE has been excellent and effective over the years. Precisely because of this, we expected much more from FIDE, to act as a responsible body that honours the agreements it makes with us, and we were disappointed!!"Despite the setback, Barkai insisted the controversy would not derail his team's ambitions in Samarkand.Asked about his expectations for the remainder of the event, he added, "The Israeli teams have performed very well so far in the Olympiad and will continue to fight with all their strength and ability to reach around 15th place. articles.title: In 2021, Roger Federer’s Wimbledon outfit and racket had a £30,000 estimate; his 2007 Rafael Nadal final memorabilia sold for £187,500
articles.summary: International Sports News: Roger Federer’s match-worn outfit and racket from his famous 2007 Wimbledon final against Rafael Nadal have been sold for £187,500 at Christie’s in Lo.
articles.body: Roger Federer’s match-worn outfit and racket from his famous 2007 Wimbledon final against Rafael Nadal have been sold for £187,500 at Christie’s in London. The items came directly from one of the biggest matches of Federer’s career, when he beat Nadal in five sets to win his fifth straight Wimbledon title. What made the auction lot even more special was the fact that both pieces were used during that final, giving collectors a direct connection to a major moment in Federer’s Grand Slam career. The sale was part of a charity auction featuring memorabilia from Federer’s career, with proceeds supporting the Roger Federer Foundation.A Wimbledon final remembered for Roger Federer and Rafael NadalThe 2007 Wimbledon final brought together two players who were already becoming the defining names of their generation. Federer was the reigning Wimbledon champion and had won the tournament four years in a row before arriving at the All England Club that summer. Nadal, meanwhile, had already established himself as one of Federer’s biggest rivals, and their meetings were attracting huge attention from tennis fans around the world.Federer wore the white Nike playing outfit and used the Wilson racket during the final against Nadal. The match lasted nearly four hours and went to five sets before Federer finally secured the victory. It was another difficult contest between the two players, but Federer managed to come through and lift the Wimbledon trophy once again.The win meant more than simply adding another Grand Slam title to his career. Federer had entered the tournament trying to win Wimbledon for the fifth consecutive time, something he had already come close to achieving in the previous years. By defeating Nadal in the final, he completed that run and added another important achievement to his record at the tournament.The final also became another important chapter in the Federer-Nadal rivalry. Their matches were closely followed because of the contrast between their playing styles and the importance of the tournaments in which they met. Wimbledon was particularly significant because it was one of the places where Federer had enjoyed some of his greatest success.That history is part of what gives the auction items their value today. The Nike outfit and Wilson racket are not simply old pieces of tennis equipment. They were used during a Grand Slam final that Federer won after a five-set battle with Nadal, making them directly connected to one of the most memorable moments of his Wimbledon career.For collectors, that kind of connection can make a piece of sports memorabilia much more meaningful. A signed item can be valuable on its own, but an object that can be linked to a particular championship match carries another layer of history. In this case, the outfit and racket were connected to a Wimbledon final that helped define Federer’s dominance at the tournament.Federer’s match-worn outfit and racket head to auctionThe items eventually became part of The Roger Federer Collection, a series of auctions featuring memorabilia from different stages of his Grand Slam career. Christie’s in London offered the Wimbledon outfit and racket as one of the lots, with an initial estimate of between £30,000 and £50,000.The lot included Federer’s signed white Nike playing outfit, which featured gold details, along with the Wilson racket he used during the 2007 Wimbledon final. Both pieces were connected directly to the match against Nadal, making the lot different from ordinary Federer memorabilia that may only carry his signature or name.The auction result went far beyond Christie’s original estimate. The items sold for £187,500, which was more than three times the top end of the £50,000 estimate. That meant the final price was £137,500 above the high end of the initial valuation.The result showed the level of interest in memorabilia tied to major moments from Federer’s career. The connection to the 2007 Wimbledon final was especially important because it combined several elements that collectors look for in sports memorabilia. The items were match-worn, they came from a Grand Slam final, they were connected to a victory and they were associated with Nadal, one of Federer’s most important rivals.The outfit also carried Federer’s signature, adding another direct connection to the player. However, the main importance of the lot came from its history on the court. Federer had actually worn the clothing and used the racket during the final, rather than the pieces being simply produced as merchandise connected to the tournament.That distinction helped make the lot a particularly notable part of the collection. The items could be traced back to a specific match rather than being linked only to a tournament or season.The auction also gave tennis fans and collectors an opportunity to own something from a period when Federer was regularly winning the biggest titles in the sport. His fifth consecutive Wimbledon championship was one of the major achievements of his career, and these objects were present during that victory.The £187,500 price therefore reflected the history attached to the pieces. Instead of being valued only as clothing and sporting equipment, they became physical reminders of a championship final that remains closely associated with Federer and Nadal.The Wimbledon memorabilia was sold for charityThe auction was not simply about selling valuable sports memorabilia. Federer donated the items for The Roger Federer Collection, with the auctions created to benefit the Roger Federer Foundation.The foundation supports education initiatives in Switzerland and countries across Southern Africa. Through the collection, Federer was able to turn important pieces from his playing career into funds for the foundation’s work.The 2021 collection included a wide range of memorabilia from Federer’s career. Clothing, rackets, shoes and other items connected to his appearances at all four Grand Slam tournaments were included in the sales. This meant that the collection covered different parts of Federer’s career rather than focusing on only one tournament.Christie’s said that the live auction in London and the online sale together raised £3,429,125. Every lot in the collection was sold, and the combined result was more than three times the low estimate set before the sales.That made the auction significant beyond the individual £187,500 Wimbledon sale. Each piece had its own story from Federer’s career, but the wider collection allowed those stories to support the work of his foundation.For the Wimbledon lot, the connection to the 2007 final made it particularly easy to identify the moment behind the memorabilia. The outfit was what Federer wore on court, while the racket was the equipment he used during his five-set victory over Nadal.The charity aspect also gave the sale another purpose. Collectors were not simply purchasing pieces of tennis history; their purchases were contributing to the foundation that Federer established to support education.The collection also showed how memorabilia from a long sporting career can carry value beyond its original use. A racket that was once a piece of equipment used during a match could later become a collector’s item because of the history attached to that particular day. The same was true of the clothing Federer wore while competing for another Wimbledon title.Federer went on to finish his career with 20 Grand Slam singles titles, making the memorabilia from his major victories an important part of his sporting legacy. Wimbledon was one of the tournaments most closely associated with his career, and the 2007 final was one of the many major occasions that helped build that reputation.Another Federer Grand Slam lot reaches the same £187,500 priceThe Wimbledon outfit and racket were not the only pieces from Federer’s Grand Slam career to reach £187,500 during the charity collection. His outfit and racket from the 2009 French Open final sold for the same amount.That match had a different place in Federer’s career because it gave him his first Roland-Garros title. He defeated Robin Söderling in the final to complete a career Grand Slam, adding the French Open trophy to the Wimbledon, US Open and Australian Open titles he had already won.The two lots therefore represented different major moments from Federer’s career. The Wimbledon pieces came from his fifth consecutive championship at the tournament, while the French Open items came from the final in which he finally won his first Roland-Garros title.Both lots reaching £187,500 showed the interest in memorabilia connected to specific Grand Slam victories. The value was not simply tied to Federer being a famous tennis player. Each item had a clear story behind it and could be connected to an important championship match.The Wimbledon pieces had another element that made their story particularly recognizable. They came from a final against Nadal, whose rivalry with Federer became one of the most important storylines in modern tennis. Their 2007 Wimbledon meeting was one of many major matches between the two players, but this particular contest ended with Federer extending his run of Wimbledon championships.For collectors, the combination of the match, the opponent, the championship and Federer’s fifth consecutive Wimbledon title gave the items a clear place in tennis history. The fact that they were match-worn and used during the final made that connection even more direct.The £187,500 sale also turned the outfit and racket into far more than pieces of sports equipment. They now represent a specific day in Federer’s career, when he faced Nadal on the Wimbledon stage and completed another successful title defense.At the same time, the money raised through the charity collection gave the memorabilia a purpose beyond collecting. Items that had once been part of Federer’s playing career were sold to help support education initiatives through his foundation.Federer’s 2007 Wimbledon victory remains an important part of his career, and the auction has now added another chapter to the story of the final. His signed Nike outfit and Wilson racket were worn and used during the five-set match, kept as pieces of his career and eventually offered to collectors through Christie’s.The £187,500 sale price reflects the history attached to those objects, while their inclusion in The Roger Federer Collection means the memorabilia also played a role in supporting the charitable work of the Roger Federer Foundation. For tennis fans, the items offer a physical link to Federer’s fifth straight Wimbledon title and another memorable meeting with Nadal, while for the foundation, their sale helped turn a piece of sporting history into support for education initiatives.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Little booing row: Real fear darts superstar 'could walk away' from sport
articles.summary: Could Luke Littler walk away from darts completely if the booing he has suffered at European tournaments continues?
articles.body:
At just 19, Luke Littler has won every major trophy in darts.

He is a multi-millionaire with lucrative sponsorship deals and his own TV show.

But has his rapid rise turned some against him?

This past weekend the teenager was once again subjected to boos and whistles from sections of the crowd as he took to the stage at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam.

What is surprising though is that it came as 'The Nuke' was on a quest to complete a darts clean sweep by becoming the first player to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year.

Littler suggested afterwards that, if the booing continues, he will not attend events held in the Netherlands.

But Samuel Gill, editor of Dartnews.com, suggests Littler's future in the sport could be at stake.

"There's a real fear that within a few years he'll just turn around and walk away from the sport," Gill told BBC Sport.

"So, I think for fans, 'Don't bite the hand that feeds you'. If people keep taunting him and don't want him to win, he might end up just walking away and not bothering anymore."

Amsterdam was the latest tournament where Littler has faced what some might describe as an overly hostile reaction from fans.

A vibrant pantomime-style atmosphere is part and parcel of the darts experience and Dutch and German crowds are amongs the most raucous - but it is clear Littler believes he has been unfairly targeted.

The referee stopped the match during his narrow win against Nathan Aspinall in the last-16 on Saturday to warn the hostile crowd about its behaviour, before play resumed.

It followed Littler also being booed during his win against home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday.

The teenager's quarter-final defeat to Jonny Clayton ended Littler's quest for the clean sweep, but the Warrington native clearly felt fans had been unduly harsh towards him.

Littler has now withdrawn from a series of upcoming events.

"Just no point in me travelling, wasting my time while I'm getting booed," said Littler.

Littler has also been jeered at numerous events in the UK.

His phenomenal rise saw him reach the PDC World Darts Championship aged just 16 in his debut year as a professional.

He captured the title the following year and the trophies, sponsorship deals and six-figure winners' cheques have continued to flow.

But increasingly so have whistles and boos during his performances.

"I don't think people expected him to reach the heights that he has so quickly," Gill said.

The darts journalist - who became aware of Littler when the sport star was 14 - says this level of attention is not just unique to the British player.

"Michael van Gerwen was the same for a long time when he dominated the sport. He barely lost a game in about five years, and he was hoovering up titles for fun and it was similar," said Gill.

"Everyone wanted to boo him and even me as a viewer before I got into this role, growing up watching Van Gerwen, I wanted him to lose because it's something different for the sport every single week."

Currently ranked number one in the world, Littler is so far ahead of his closest rivals that he already has the advantage of only having to play in selective tournaments.

His boycott threat could end up being a blow to tournament organisers.

"They don't like him because he's that good. And he's got a bit of swagger to him," said Karl Holden secretary of St Helen's Darts Academy - where Littler honed his skills from the age of nine.

"Luke's got a bit of a character to him. For me, he's the ultimate professional. He might give a little bit of the large sometimes, but you need that, otherwise darts would be totally boring."

It seems remarkable that the future of Littler's career in the sport is even being debated.

More so when you consider his age and the fact he only turned professional two years ago.

However, Gill believes that Littler's rapid haul of trophies, coupled with the huge amounts of money now in the sport, could result in the teenager leaving in the next "four to five years" should the boos and whistles continue.

Gill believes Littler's impact on the darting world is immeasurable.

Tickets to events featuring him are often sold out, applications to darting academies are reported to be at an all-time high and the Briton has transcended the sport.

Gill therefore feels that, if Littler was to walk away, the sport would be the real loser.

"He's the one who is bringing this sport to a completely different level. Nowadays, he is back-page news wherever you go," Gill said.

"He might just decide 'I just want a quiet life now and just live off his money'."

Littler has barely known anything other than winning. His challenged now is maintaining that victorious streak while keeping fans - whose interest helps fund his prize money - happy.

Tricky when some are paying with the hope of seeing him lose.

"If he was on that stage, everybody liked him and he just threw darts, I think I'd get bored of watching him," Holden said.

articles.title: El drama del menor marroquí escondido en el bus del Valladolid desde Ceuta: "Estaba muy magullado"
articles.standfirst: El responsable de la portavocía del conjunto pucelano relata en 'Otra Ronda' cómo vivió la expedición el momento en el que descubrieron al menor escondido en los bajos del autobús
articles.summary: El responsable de la portavocía del conjunto pucelano relata en 'Otra Ronda' cómo vivió la expedición el momento en el que descubrieron al menor escondido en los bajos del autobús
articles.body: La expedición del Real Valladolid vivió una situación insólita durante su regreso a casa después del partido ante el Ceuta. Un menor marroquí de 17 años había conseguido esconderse en los bajos de uno de los autobuses del conjunto pucelano para cruzar desde Ceuta a la Península y permaneció allí durante buena parte del trayecto. Jorge Santiago, responsable de la portavocía del club, contó en 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA, programa presentado por Carlos Vicente 'Chitu', cómo fueron aquellos momentos. El Valladolid viajaba en dos autobuses después de haber cruzado el Estrecho en el vehículo oficial. "Nada más pasar el desvío de Jerez, me llaman desde el primer autobús para decirme que están escuchando ruidos", explicó Santiago. El club se puso inmediatamente en contacto con la Guardia Civil y decidió detener la marcha en un área de servicio. Fue entonces cuando descubrieron al menor en los bajos del vehículo. "El chico sale, más que sale, cae, porque la verdad que estaba bastante magullado y bastante mala pinta en ese momento", relató el portavoz. El joven pidió agua y la expedición trató de ayudarle mientras esperaba la llegada de las autoridades. "Le pudimos dar agua, le pudimos dar de comer, le ayudamos con lo que pudimos. La verdad que los chavales estuvieron fantásticos", añadió. La barrera del idioma complicó inicialmente la comunicación con el menor, que únicamente hablaba árabe. Poncho intentó comunicarse con él en francés y, posteriormente, una amiga que hablaba árabe pudo ayudar a establecer contacto con el joven para tranquilizarle. Además, el médico del Real Valladolid realizó un primer reconocimiento y, ante las molestias que manifestaba, especialmente en la espalda, se solicitó una ambulancia. Mientras esperaban a la Guardia Civil y a los servicios sanitarios, los jugadores permanecieron junto al menor. Finalmente, la ambulancia llegó y el joven quedó bajo custodia de las autoridades mientras la expedición blanquivioleta continuaba su viaje hacia Valladolid. Santiago reconoció que lo vivido provocó un fuerte impacto entre los integrantes del equipo. "Jugarse la vida de esa manera a todos nos impactó cuando lo vimos en directo", señaló. El portavoz del Valladolid puso el foco en el riesgo que había asumido el menor al viajar escondido en una zona tan peligrosa del autobús. "Podría ser el chico que se hubiera cansado de estar agarrado ahí y que le hubieran fallado las fuerzas y desgraciadamente le hubiéramos atropellado con nuestro autobús", explicó. Para Santiago, que el desenlace fuera diferente hizo que la experiencia adquiriera todavía más peso una vez que la expedición retomó el viaje. El portavoz del Valladolid también admitió que el episodio le llevó a reflexionar en el plano personal. "Cuando ves al chico, pues tema de empatía y de humanidad, como tú bien dices, pues tienes que ayudarle", afirmó. Y añadió: "Te entran esos pensamientos de, bueno, qué suerte tenemos los que vivimos de otra manera y los que tenemos una vida, vamos a llamarlo normal para nosotros, pero para otra gente tan lejana que es capaz de jugarse su vida metiéndose debajo de un autobús para poder tener una oportunidad". Santiago reconoció que la situación vivida en Ceuta durante el fin de semana, unida a lo ocurrido durante el regreso, le hizo tomar conciencia de la complejidad del contexto. "Cuando lo ves en primera persona a un chico que es un crío, que ha estado agarrado allí, que ha estado jugándose la vida, pues la verdad que te impacta y te hace pensar", concluyó.

articles.title: Brewers prospect named the Southern League's most valuable player
articles.summary: Blake Burke, who finished the season with the Brewers' Class AAA team, also mashed in Class AA this year and was named Southern League MVP.
articles.body:
Blake Burke may no longer be a member of the Class AA Biloxi Shuckers, but the Milwaukee Brewers ' slugging first base prospect left a mark.

Burke was named the Southern League most valuable player Sept. 21, a nod to Burke's incredible season before an August promotion to Class AAA Nashville.

He was joined by teammates Jesús Made, Josh Adamczewski and Andrew Fischer on the 2026 Southern League All-Star Team . All are highly regarded prospects in the Brewers organization.

Burke hit 30 home runs at Biloxi – giving him a franchise-record 41 in his Double-A career – and led the league in batting average (.285) and OPS (.970). He became the first Southern League player with a 30-homer season since Wisconsin native Adam Brett Walker in 2015, and Burke needed just 88 games to reach that threshold.

All told, Burke played 96 games at Biloxi and stole 28 bases despite his 6-foot-3, 236-pound frame. Though he struggled in 31 games at Nashville (.635 OPS, four homers), his overall numbers for the year were still strong (.263 average, .889 OPS, 34 homers, 29 steals).

The 23-year-old left-handed bat, a 2024 Brewers first-round pick, is regarded as the No. 12 prospect in the organization by MLB Pipeline.

Burke and the rest of the Shuckers hit a franchise-record 178 home runs in 2026, shattering the old record of 154. Fischer, the Southern League all-star at third base, had a lot to do with it by parking 28 homers in 72 games with the Shuckers, with a 1.026 OPS for his portion of the season at Class AA.

Made, regarded as the top prospect in baseball, made the all-star team as a shortstop and spent all season with Biloxi. He finished with 14 homers, 91 RBIs, 37 steals and a .774 OPS. The 19-year-old's RBI count was the most in franchise history, breaking the mark of 90 by Jackson Chourio in 2023, and led the league.

Adamczewski, regarded as the No. 3 prospect in the organization, played in 66 games after promotion and made the Southern League all-star team as the left fielder. He had an .837 OPS in Biloxi with nine homers and eight steals. He started his career with a 12-game hitting streak, the longest stretch by any Shucker this season.

Burke is the first Brewers minor-leaguer to win a league MVP award since 2022, when both Jackson Chourio (Carolina League) and Jakson Reetz (Southern League) earned MVP honors.

Reetz, a catcher signed by the Brewers in the offseason before the 2022 season, left after they designated him for assignment in August of that season, and he elected free agency after clearing waivers. He had briefly gotten to the big leagues for two at-bats with Washington in 2021 and got back in 2024 with San Francisco for 14 at-bats.

Other Brewers prospects to win league player of the year awards at the top four levels are:

Mario Feliciano (2019, Carolina League with Carolina)

Corey Ray (2018, Southern League with Biloxi)

Hunter Morris (2012, Southern League with Huntsville)
