articles.title: Kickoff time, TV options set for Georgia football's game vs. Vanderbilt
articles.summary: Georgia football’s game vs. Vanderbilt on Saturday, Oct. 3, now has a kickoff time and TV network options laid out. Here are the details.
articles.body:
The No. 2 Bulldogs ' game against Vanderbilt on Saturday, Oct. 3, is set for a start between noon and 12:45 p.m. and will be broadcast nationally on either ABC, ESPN or the SEC Network, according to an announcement Monday by the university.

The final determination will be solidified after Georgia plays Oklahoma on Saturday, Sept. 26.

The Bulldogs and Commodores have played 83 times, dating back to 1893, with Georgia taking the last six victories. The last time they met at Sanford Stadium was 2022, which Georgia won 55-0.

Tickets for the game start at $129 on StubHub .

The Commodores (3-0) came from behind with three seconds remaining in regulation to beat NC State 35-31 in week 3. They received 29 votes towards this week's US LBM Coaches Poll but are not ranked. Vanderbilt plays at Jordan-Hare Stadium on Saturday against Auburn, with kickoff set for 3:15 p.m.

Georgia, which thumped Arkansas 45-17 on Saturday, Sept. 19, faces its first home conference foe in Oklahoma on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. It's the first time the Sooners will play in Sanford Stadium, with their one and only meeting being the 2017 Rose Bowl, which Georgia won 54-48 in double overtime.

articles.title: Ohio is filled with blue-chip talent in the 2027 cycle
articles.summary: There are 17 blue-chip prospects in the state of Ohio in the 2027 cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking, a weighted average that utilizes all major...
articles.body:
There are 17 blue-chip prospects in the state of Ohio in the 2027 cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , a weighted average that utilizes all major recruiting media companies. It's the second cycle in a row that the state totes more than 15.

The Buckeye State remains among the best in the Midwest when it comes to consistently producing high school stars and college prospects. This cycle, there's droves of talent on the offensive line and in the secondary.

All 17 of the four-stars are committed and have been for some time. Naturally, a majority of the best in the state are headed for the Big Ten. Rivals breaks down the top 10 2027 prospects in Ohio and where they're pledged, as of Sept. 21.

Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 19 NATL. (No. 4 WR) School: Wayne

Scouting Summary: "Speedy playmaker who is highly dangerous after the catch. Measured in at around 5-foot-11, 190 pounds prior to his senior season. Steadily gained mass and filled out his frame, with over 20 pounds of weight gained from his sophomore to junior years. Has elite top-end speed as the top sprinter in the state of Ohio. Has personal best times of 10.35 seconds and 20.79 seconds in the 100 and 200 meters respectively. Won state titles in both events as a junior. Also shows that top-end speed in the combine setting. Identified as a top wide receiver prospect early in the cycle. Shows flashes of that speed on Friday nights. Has the ability to take the top off of defenses with a top gear that can separate against cornerbacks on vertical routes. Does a nice job working back to the quarterback on broken plays. Dangerous with the ball in his hands and a threat to score every time he touches the ball.

…Combination of speed and filled out frame makes him tough for defenders to bring down. Dangerous in the quick game adds value as a ball carrier. Doubles as a strong return man, capable of taking it to the house. Finished his junior season with 73 catches for 1,009 yards and 10 touchdowns. Saw his efficiency dip a bit (13.8 yards per catch). Does not always play to his timed speed, especially in neutral settings. Ball skills register as solid to good and can be improved. Projects as a multi-faceted playmaker who can take advantage of manufactured touches at the college level with the upside to grow into a more complete receiver with continued development."

Rivals Industry Ranking: No. 55 NATL. (No. 6 IOL) School: Liberty Center

Scouting Summary: "Elite athlete along the offensive line who looks like one of the best movers among the 2027 interior offensive line prospects. Listed at around 6-foot-5, 270 pounds. Can absolutely move at his size. Excellent when working as a puller and moving to the second level. Has the speed to reach cornerbacks when blocking on screen passes to the outside. A weapon in the run game with his ability to work to the second level. Has quality pop in his hands and works to finish blocks. Also flashes outstanding reactive quickness in pass protection, easily mirroring pass rushers with his explosive lateral agility.

…Flashes his athleticism as a defensive lineman, as well. Participates in the shot put (43-3 feet) and discus (142 feet) in track and field. Will need to continue adding mass to his frame, but has the upside to be one of the top interior offensive linemen in the cycle with the versatility to play any of the five spots on the front."

articles.title: 3 Rockets on hottest trade candidate seats entering 2026-27 NBA training camp
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets enter training camp with championship expectations, enviable depth and an inevitable numbers problem. Kevin Durant, Amen Thompson, Alper...
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets enter training camp with championship expectations, enviable depth and an inevitable numbers problem. Kevin Durant, Amen Thompson , Alperen Sengun , Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason form a well-defined core, while the offseason additions of Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic created even more competition for rotation minutes.

General manager Rafael Stone does not need to force a trade before opening night. However, Houston appears positioned to pursue another significant move, whether during the season or next summer. If the Rockets decide their current roster needs another star or cleaner positional balance, three players stand out as the most logical trade candidates.

Sheppard is Houston's most valuable realistic trade chip and that distinction places him squarely on the hot seat. The former No. 3 overall pick remains only 22 years old, carries a manageable $11.1 million salary and offers the shooting upside that almost every modern offense covets.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The problem is opportunity. VanVleet is returning, Smart joined on a two-year contract, Thompson recently received a five-year extension and Bogdanovic adds another proven perimeter option. Sheppard could still become Houston's long-term answer at guard, but the backcourt is crowded enough to make his role uncertain.

That also makes him the premium piece in any blockbuster package. A rebuilding team would likely prefer Sheppard's upside to one of Houston's older veterans. The Rockets should not shop him merely to clear minutes, but if an established star becomes available, Sheppard is the young player most likely to headline the offer. ESPN's Brian Windhorst has already described Houston as primed for another trade, with Sheppard identified as a top asset who could be moved.

VanVleet carries the greatest combination of contract utility and basketball uncertainty. The 32-year-old exercised his $25 million player option after missing the entire 2025-26 season because of a torn right ACL. He is expected to return, but training camp will reveal whether he can still defend, create separation and handle starter-level minutes after a lost season.

His expiring salary makes him useful in trade construction, especially if Houston targets a high-priced guard or wing. VanVleet also no longer possesses the implied no-trade protection he held under his previous contract structure. That does not mean the Rockets want him gone; his leadership, ball control and playoff experience remain valuable to a contender.

Still, Smart provides insurance and Thompson deserves more on-ball responsibility. If VanVleet looks diminished—or if Smart proves capable of organizing the second unit—Houston could use VanVleet's salary to rebalance the roster before the deadline. His camp performance may determine whether he remains indispensable or becomes an expensive matching contract.

Capela faces the clearest rotation squeeze. Sengun is the franchise center, Steven Adams remains a trusted physical backup and Capela enters camp as the likely third big. Carrying three traditional centers makes sense during the regular season, but it becomes harder to justify when playoff rotations shrink and Durant or Smith can absorb occasional small-ball minutes.

Capela still supplies rebounding, rim protection and vertical spacing. Those skills could interest teams with fragile center depth, while his $7 million salary is relatively easy to move. Houston reportedly received interest in Capela before the 2026 trade deadline, although nothing became concrete.

Unlike Sheppard, Capela would not headline a star trade. Unlike VanVleet, he would not be needed primarily for salary matching. He is simply the veteran whose role appears most replaceable.

Sheppard is the biggest swing, VanVleet is the most important training-camp evaluation and Capela is the cleanest trade. Houston can keep all three, but a championship team rarely carries this much overlapping depth all season. If Stone makes another move, one of them will probably provide the pathway.

articles.title: Lakers Cut Ties With Former Celtics Draft Pick One Day After Signing Him
articles.summary: Anton Watson's latest NBA opportunity lasted one day.
articles.body:
Anton Watson 's time with the Los Angeles Lakers didn't last long.

On Thursday, the Lakers announced that they signed Watson to an Exhibit 10 contract. The following day, the Lakers announced that they had signed two more players and waived Watson.

After five seasons at Gonzaga, the Boston Celtics selected Watson with the No. 54 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, one pick ahead of Bronny James . Watson signed a two-way contract with the Celtics but was waived before appearing in a single NBA game for Boston.

Watson spent most of his time with the Celtics organization in the G League, playing for the Maine Celtics.

Watson was claimed off waivers by the Knicks after the Celtics waived him and appeared in nine games for New York. He then spent the 2025-26 season in the G League, playing for the Lakers' affiliate, the South Bay Lakers.

The Lakers' decision to waive Watson one day after signing him appears to be part of an effort to keep him in their G League system with the newly relocated Coachella Valley Lakers.

Watson appeared in 50 games (34 starts) for South Bay last season. He averaged 11.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.4 steals in 27.3 minutes per game.

articles.title: Patriots’ safety depth to be tested after Craig Woodson, Dell Pettus injuries
articles.summary: New England’s practice squad safeties might be counted on while Woodson and Pettus are out.
articles.body:
Amid a handful of injuries, the New England Patriots lost a pair of safeties in Craig Woodson and Dell Pettus during Sunday's win over the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Woodson appeared to suffer his shoulder injury with 9:54 remaining in the third quarter as he lowered his left side to tackle Steelers running back Rico Dowdle . A heavy collision left Woodson dangling his left arm.

After playing the next third down snap to end the series, he left the field and visited the blue medical tent before departing to the locker room. He was ruled out and was then seen wearing a sling in the post game looker room.

Pettus, meanwhile, suffered his ankle injury on a second quarter punt.

As the Patriots now begin their preparation for the Jaguars , head coach Mike Vrabel noted the team will likely need safeties on the practice squad to step up.

"We have guys on the practice squad. I think some of the veteran practice squad guys are going to factor in this week," Vrabel said. "I know that Mike Brown has been with us since the spring, and I think that's the balance that you weigh with the practice squad. We've talked about that. You have some young guys that you're looking to develop, some veteran guys that have played in games that are preparing as a starter and that'll be ready to go.

"So as the week unfolds, we'll have to make sure that everybody's ready to go. If guys can't end up making it, then however we sign guys or elevate guys."

Brown is one of the Patriots' most experienced practice squad players, signing with New England this offseason with 38 career games under his belt. That included playing in 9 games at safety for Vrabel's Titans in 2023.

New England's developmental team also includes second-year safety Elliott Davison, who originally joined the team following training camp.

With Woodson and Pettus leaving Sunday's game early, safety Jaylen Reed was thurst into a larger role.

After being acquired in a trade for Kayshon Boutte this August, Reed did not play a defensive snap in the season opener. The 23-year old, who has seen an increased comfort level in the defense, was called upon to play 28 snaps (40%) against the Steelers.

"I think Jaylen has done a nice job. He's worked hard," Vrabel said. "He got put in there – again, we have to be ready to go. He had some plays that were good. He's helped us in the kicking game. He would go in there at PP [punt protector], that's not an easy thing to do, so I'm glad that he was prepared and ready to go."

Jayden Daniels 's injury was the major storyline for the Commanders in Sunday's loss to the Cowboys, but the quarterback was not the only member of the team to suffer an injury.

Head coach Dan Quinn said at his Monday press conference, via multiple reporters, that defensive back Nick Cross remained in Dallas on Sunday night so he could be evaluated at a local hospital for an internal injury. Quinn said Cross was released from the hospital on Monday and is now on his way home.

Quinn did not provide any further details about Cross's injury or outlook moving forward.

Cross has started both games for the Commanders this season. He had 11 tackles in those appearances.

articles.title: 3 Cavs on hottest trade candidate seats entering 2026-27 NBA training camp
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers enter training camp with a dramatically reshaped roster and unmistakable championship pressure. Donovan Mitchell received a four-year...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers enter training camp with a dramatically reshaped roster and unmistakable championship pressure. Donovan Mitchell received a four-year maximum extension, James Harden returned on a three-year deal and Cleveland sacrificed an unprotected 2031 first-round pick to acquire Peyton Watson .

Those moves strengthened the Cavaliers, but they also made the roster expensive and reduced future flexibility. Cleveland carries approximately $206.7 million in active salary and sits only narrowly below the first apron. If the new formula stumbles, management may need to move a useful player rather than wait for the situation to correct itself. Three Cavaliers stand out as the likeliest trade candidates.

Allen owns the hottest seat because he combines genuine trade value with a salary large enough to facilitate a significant deal. The 28-year-old center will earn $28 million this season as the first year of his three-year extension begins. That contract is substantial, but it remains reasonable for a productive starting center in his prime.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cleveland would not move Allen simply to cut costs. He averaged 19.7 points and 10 rebounds while shooting 71 percent after Feb. 1 last season, providing elite efficiency and reliable interior production. His screening, finishing and rebounding complement Harden's pick-and-roll creativity, while his size allows Evan Mobley to avoid handling every bruising center matchup.

The larger question is whether the Cavaliers can maximize Mobley while continuing to play two non-shooting bigs. Watson's arrival gives coach Kenny Atkinson another long, athletic defender, potentially making smaller lineups more appealing. If Cleveland starts slowly or needs another perimeter creator, Allen is its clearest path toward obtaining one. He has already been ranked among the NBA's leading trade targets, with reports identifying him as Cleveland's most likely major piece to move if the team underachieves.

Merrill is not a problematic fit. In fact, his movement shooting is especially valuable beside Mitchell, Harden, Mobley and Allen. His inclusion is about roster economics and marketability rather than performance.

The 30-year-old guard is owed roughly $9.2 million this season and remains under contract through 2028-29. That manageable deal could appeal to contenders seeking dependable shooting without sacrificing a major salary slot. It also makes Merrill useful as matching money if Cleveland pursues a more versatile wing or packages several contracts for a larger upgrade.

The Cavaliers have enough young perimeter players to contemplate that move. Jaylon Tyson , Tyrese Proctor , Meleek Thomas and Craig Porter Jr. all need developmental minutes, while Watson and Mario Hezonja further crowd the wing rotation. Cleveland should not dump Merrill for financial relief, but his specialized skill and affordable contract make him one of the roster's easiest veterans to trade.

Tyson is the most complicated name because Cleveland should want to keep him. The 23-year-old averaged 13.2 points and 5.1 rebounds across 66 games last season while shooting 44.6 percent from three. He also remains on a team-controlled rookie contract, giving the Cavaliers inexpensive production at a time when their stars are becoming extremely costly.

That value is precisely why rival teams would ask for him. Clubs previously contacting Cleveland reportedly showed interest in Tyson alongside Mobley, Allen and former Cavalier Max Strus . With Watson now occupying the long-term wing role on a four-year, $88 million contract, Tyson's route to consistent touches could become narrower.

Trading Tyson merely because the rotation is crowded would be shortsighted. Trading him as the central young asset in a deal for a proven difference-maker would be defensible. His shooting, age and low salary give him more appeal than Cleveland's fringe prospects.

Allen is the most likely centerpiece of a major shake-up, Merrill is the cleanest supporting asset and Tyson is the premium developmental chip. Training camp will determine whether Cleveland's depth fits together—or whether one of those players becomes the price of fixing its next problem.

articles.title: NFL news: Irvin hates on trend after Williams, Daniels add to injury woes around league
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has quickly become one of the league’s most electrifying playmakers, earning significant praise from...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has quickly become one of the league's most electrifying playmakers , earning significant praise from legendary NFL analysts, like Michael Irvin , who are astonished by his elite agility, exceptional route-running, and incredible ability to change direction seamlessly on the field.

While individual brilliance continues to light up highlight reels across the league, a darker narrative has emerged during the early season due to a wave of devastating injuries affecting marquee quarterbacks like Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels . As the physical toll on players increases, Hall of Famer Michael Irvin delivered a passionate critique on Pat McAfee's show regarding the current practices in roster management and preseason preparation. He specifically targeted the trend of resting star players entirely before Week 1.

Expressing his frustration with how teams handle training camps and preparation, Irvin took to social media, stating: "I have said this so many times… I don't know how you can ramp up without ramping up. How do you start the season without having any game practice at all?"

Irvin argued that keeping players out of competitive snaps during the preseason leaves their bodies unprepared for the physical demands and speed of live regular-season action, which contributes to the alarming rise in soft-tissue strains and severe injuries in the opening weeks. As medical staffs around the league scramble to address these injuries and superstars deal with setbacks, the debate over how teams condition their athletes before the season has intensified.

With the league facing increasing scrutiny over player health and preparation schedules, coaches and executives may soon need to reconsider whether protecting players is actually doing more harm than good.

articles.title: Chiefs news: Travis Kelce given head turning Kyle Shanahan comparison
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs walked out of Week 2 with an overtime 33-30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on “Sunday Night Football.” Travis Kelce looked like the b...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs walked out of Week 2 with an overtime 33-30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on "Sunday Night Football." Travis Kelce looked like the best tight end in the league once again, giving the offense a major boost against Indy. His play caught the attention of Dan Orlovsky , as the former NFL quarterback compared Kelce to San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan.

Orlovsky explained his reasoning during a guest appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show." The popular football analyst claims that Kelce plays football similarly to how Shanahan calls plays . In that, the 36-year-old tight end just finds the space in the defense. That's something Shanahan tends to do when dialing up plays for his 49ers offense.

"When I watch Kelce play right now, I feel like I'm watching Kyle Shanahan call offensive plays," Orlovsky said. "I think one of the things about Kyle is so great is he understands rules of a defense, and where they can and cannot be. I feel Travis has got that same understanding. Like, he just knows, okay, 'Defensive structure is this. That means you guys can't be there. My route might say 10 yards, but why wouldn't I break it to seven yards?' And there's so many plays where [Kelce] just kind of just goes to space."

Travis Kelce erupted for 101 yards and a touchdown off nine receptions against the Colts on Sunday night. He led Kansas City in targets from quarterback Patrick Mahomes with 11. There were multiple times throughout the contest when Mahomes found the four-time First-Team All-Pro wide open, as Indianapolis had a difficult time covering Kelce throughout the game.

The 14-year veteran and the Chiefs will aim to remain undefeated in their next game in Week 3. Kansas City will fly Southeast for a road game against the Miami Dolphins .
